16	## Problem
17	
18	`sentry-alert-consumer` runs on nukeprod, and `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` mirrors `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(CONSUMER_TAG)` into `docker.prod.nuke.benjamin-borbe.de:443`. 19	
20	The arm is not a straight copy. Three properties of this repo make a naive paste fail at runtime rather than at review:
21	
22	- **`VERSION` is defaulted at parse time.** `Makefile.docker` opens with `ifeq ($(VERSION),) VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags …) endif`, so by the time any guard could read `$(origin VERSION)` the variable is `file` and an omitted tag silently resolves to the last released tag. A cluster arm that inherited that default would republish a released tag over itself, irreversibly.
23	- **`Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`.** `Makefile:3` is the include and `Makefile:5` is `SERVICE = sentry-alert-consumer`, so any parse-time use of `$(SERVICE)` inside `Makefile.docker` — an `ifeq`, a `:=` — evaluates empty and composes `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
24	- **The image build resolves dependencies from `vendor/`.** The Dockerfile runs `go build -mod=vendor`, `vendor/` is gitignored, and `origin/master` carries no `vendor/` directory. A Job that clones the repo has no `vendor/`, so the build fails before it starts.
25	
26	A fourth property only bites the lane rather than the build, and it was settled by measurement on this repo rather than by reading the docs. `.dark-factory.yaml` on `origin/master` carries `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true`, and a cluster run on exactly that config failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/001-spec-001-docs-build-section.md: no such file or directory` — the same signature recorded on `obsidian-redirector` PR #15. The identical spec run under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` completed all three prompts. So `direct` is the working shape here and `worktree` is the regression, whatever the two older "completed siblings" carry. `autoRelease: false` stays: it keeps the release manual, which this repo wants.

152	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
153	|---|---|---|
154	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown cluster or context | The runner fails before applying anything and lists the accepted values | Re-run with a listed target; no Job exists to clean up |
155	| `VERSION` omitted on the cluster arm | Refusal before the Job is created, naming `VERSION` | Re-run passing `VERSION=<scratch-tag>` |

157	| `REF` exists locally but was never pushed | The clone init container fails: the ref does not exist on `origin` | Push the branch or commit, then re-run |
158	| The clone's commit epoch differs from the locally derived one | The build container refuses before `buildctl` runs and names both epochs | `git fetch`, then re-run |
159	| A Job with the derived name already exists in `build` | The runner refuses and names the existing Job rather than overwriting it | Delete the finished Job, then re-run |
160	| The runner is interrupted after `apply` | The Job keeps running in the cluster while the local invocation exits; the next run then hits the existing-Job refusal | Inspect `kubectlsun -n build get jobs`, read the pod's log, delete the Job once finished |

162	| The build pod is OOM-killed or throttled | The Job reports `failed`; the pod status carries `OOMKilled` or a CPU-throttling event | Raise the template's limits in the same change, or build locally for that one image |

175	- `VERSION` is caller-controlled and becomes an image tag and a Job name. The tag is whitelisted and the Job name is sanitized to a valid DNS name, truncated, and stripped of trailing separators.

## Summary

- This repo's image can currently be produced on one machine only: the Mac.
- Its sibling repos can also build their image inside a Kubernetes cluster, unattended, from any committed ref.
- Add that second build path here as an arm beside the existing local one, leaving the local command and tag as they are.
- The cluster arm builds a named commit as a Kubernetes Job and pushes the result to `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`, the repository nuke's mirror step copies into the private registry the deployment pulls from.
- Two supporting edits make the arm reachable: the image must build from a fresh clone with no `vendor/`, and the dark-factory lane config must stop using the shape that is known to lose commits.

## Problem

`sentry-alert-consumer` runs on nukeprod, and `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` mirrors `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(CONSUMER_TAG)` into `docker.prod.nuke.benjamin-borbe.de:443`. Every image that mirror copies is cut by hand on this Mac today: `Makefile.docker` carries only the local `docker build` path, and `hack/` does not exist. Nothing else can produce this image, so a release while the operator is away from this machine cannot happen.

The arm is not a straight copy. Three properties of this repo make a naive paste fail at runtime rather than at review:

- **`VERSION` is defaulted at parse time.** `Makefile.docker` opens with `ifeq ($(VERSION),) VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags …) endif`, so by the time any guard could read `$(origin VERSION)` the variable is `file` and an omitted tag silently resolves to the last released tag. A cluster arm that inherited that default would republish a released tag over itself, irreversibly.
- **`Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`.** `Makefile:3` is the include and `Makefile:5` is `SERVICE = sentry-alert-consumer`, so any parse-time use of `$(SERVICE)` inside `Makefile.docker` — an `ifeq`, a `:=` — evaluates empty and composes `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
- **The image build resolves dependencies from `vendor/`.** The Dockerfile runs `go build -mod=vendor`, `vendor/` is gitignored, and `origin/master` carries no `vendor/` directory. A Job that clones the repo has no `vendor/`, so the build fails before it starts.

A fourth property only bites the lane rather than the build, and it was settled by measurement on this repo rather than by reading the docs. `.dark-factory.yaml` on `origin/master` carries `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true`, and a cluster run on exactly that config failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/001-spec-001-docs-build-section.md: no such file or directory` — the same signature recorded on `obsidian-redirector` PR #15. The identical spec run under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` completed all three prompts. So `direct` is the working shape here and `worktree` is the regression, whatever the two older "completed siblings" carry. `autoRelease: false` stays: it keeps the release manual, which this repo wants.

## Goal

`make build` on this repo produces the image locally exactly as it does today, and `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` produces it inside that cluster as a Kubernetes Job, pushing `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:<tag>` — the repository nuke's mirror step consumes. Both arms work from the same checkout, and the cluster arm works from a fresh clone with no local preparation.

## Non-goals

- Changing the local arm's command or its tag. Both stay as they are. The shared Dockerfile does move to module resolution, because the cluster arm cannot build from a clone otherwise; the local arm runs the same Dockerfile and is unaffected by how dependencies are fetched.
- Pushing to the private registry from the cluster. The `buildkit-push` credential authenticates against Docker Hub only; the private copy is produced by nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` step, not by this build.
- Adding a mirror entry or bumping the pin in `bborbe/nuke`. `CONSUMER_TAG ?= v0.1.0` in `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` is already stale against the deployment's `v0.2.5`; realigning it is a deploy-side change, not this spec's.
- Touching the sibling repos — they already carry their arms.
- Building at release or tag time. This spec adds the capability; *when* a build is triggered is a separate concern. This repo sets `autoRelease: false`, so a green merge cuts no tag.
- Extracting the shared build runner into a common upstream template. The files are copied, not shared.
- Extra build knobs beyond `BUILD_TARGET`, `IMAGE`, `TAG` and `VERSION`. The copy source also carries `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION`, `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, `BUILD_REPO_URL`, `BUILD_DOCKERFILE` and `BUILD_PUSH_SECRET`. `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` in particular would reintroduce an opt-out on the refusal this spec ships, so it is not copied. The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not knobs.

## Alternatives

- **Build in GitHub Actions instead.** Rejected: CI here triggers on push or PR to `master`, so it cannot build an arbitrary committed ref on demand — which is the whole requirement. It would also put a second copy of the Docker Hub credential into GitHub secrets, where one already lives in the cluster's `build` namespace.
- **Fix the local arm instead.** Removing `Makefile.docker`'s parse-time `VERSION` default would make local builds safer, but it changes the tag the deployment already consumes and still leaves the image unbuildable without this Mac. A smaller change that does not reach the goal.
- **Reuse a shared upstream runner.** The five files are copied from `agent-task-executor` and `go-skeleton`, not vendored from a package. A shared template is the right end state, but it is its own change across every repo in the goal's target set; copying first keeps each repo's arm independently verifiable.
- **Do nothing.** See the closing section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **The local arm's command and tag are unchanged** — with no `BUILD_TARGET` set, `make -n build` prints the `docker build` recipe and no reference to `hack/build-cluster.sh`; `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack make build` exits 0 and `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:v0.2.5` exits 0 (`v0.2.5` is what `git describe --tags $(git rev-list --tags --max-count=1)` resolves today, so the tag is spelled out rather than left for the verifier to derive). Evidence: both commands' output, the recorded `docker context show` value, the exit code, and the inspected image id. ⚠️ The `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack` pin is what carries the guarantee, not the ambient state: a docker context pointed at `sun` would make a bare `make build` build on the cluster and prove nothing about the local arm.
- [ ] **Post-Deploy (Rung-2):** the cluster arm builds and pushes from a fresh clone — `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe-<timestamp>` exits 0, and `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe-<timestamp>` resolves to a digest **equal to the build log's `containerimage.digest`**. Evidence: the exit code, the Job name, the build pod's `spec.nodeName`, both digests, and `docker image inspect` on the same reference failing on this Mac with `No such image` — a stopped daemon or a malformed reference does not satisfy this.
  - `deploy_check:` `kubectlsun -n build get secret buildkit-push -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'`
  - `deploy_target:` `buildkit-push`
- [ ] **The cluster arm pushes to the repository the deploy consumes** — `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` prints `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe` on one line before it calls the runner. Evidence: the printed line alone — the digest half is AC 2's, at AC 2's own tag, so this criterion does not depend on a build that used a different tag.
- [ ] **Post-Deploy (Rung-2):** the cluster arm refuses a tag it did not receive from the caller — `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` with no `VERSION` on the command line or in the environment exits non-zero and prints a message naming `VERSION`, before any Job is applied. The refusal fires even though `Makefile.docker` otherwise defaults `VERSION` from `git describe --tags`. Evidence: the exit code, the message, and `kubectlsun -n build get jobs` showing no new Job for that run.
  - `deploy_check:` `kubectlsun -n build get secret buildkit-push -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'`
  - `deploy_target:` `buildkit-push`
- [ ] **`hack/` holds the five files and the cluster branch invokes the runner** — at the merge commit on `master`, `git ls-tree --name-only HEAD hack/` lists `build-cluster.sh`, `cluster-alias.sh`, `build-job.yaml`, `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`, and `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1 on an invocation line rather than a comment. Evidence: the five names and the count. ⚠️ The copied header comments name `BUILD_TARGET`, so a bare `grep -c BUILD_TARGET` passes on a comment alone — the `^` anchor is the probe.
- [ ] **`upload` / `clean` / `buca` stay local, refused at parse time** — `make -n buca` prints `docker push` and `docker rmi`; `make -n buca BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` exits non-zero and prints a message naming those targets as local-only. The refusal is a parse-time `$(error …)`, so it fires under `-n` where no recipe runs. Evidence: both outputs and exit codes.
- [ ] **The clone builds the image without `vendor/`** — the Dockerfile no longer forces `-mod=vendor`, so a Job that clones the repo builds the same way a developer's checkout does; `grep -c '\-mod=vendor' Dockerfile` returns 0. Evidence: that count plus the successful cluster build above, which is the behavioural half. The exact replacement flag is the implementer's call — Go's default `-mod=readonly` resolves modules without letting the build rewrite `go.mod`, so pinning `-mod=mod` would mandate an implementation choice the criterion does not need.
- [ ] **The documented build path and the lane config match reality** — `README.md` shows the exact cluster invocation `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>`, states that `buca` remains local, and records that the cluster pushes Docker Hub while nuke's mirror produces the private copy; `CHANGELOG.md` carries a bullet for this change **under** `## Unreleased`; and `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `workflow: direct` with `pr: false` — the shape that measured working on this repo — plus `defaultBranch: master` and `autoMerge: false`. Evidence: `grep -c 'BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>' README.md` ≥ 1; `grep -ci 'buca' README.md` ≥ 1; `grep -c 'MIRROR_IMAGES' README.md` ≥ 1; `awk '/^## /{s=$0} /cluster build/{print s}' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## Unreleased` (the bare `grep -c '^## Unreleased$'` alone passes at baseline and asserts nothing, and DB 8's bullet is the `cluster build` phrase); and each `.dark-factory.yaml` value is pinned rather than merely present — `grep -c '^workflow: direct$'` = 1, `^pr: false$` = 1, `^autoMerge: false$` = 1, `^autoRelease: false$` = 1, `^autoGeneratePrompts: true$` = 1, `^defaultBranch: master$` = 1 and `^validationPrompt: docs/dod\.md$` = 1, all against `.dark-factory.yaml`. Those read the working tree, so the criterion also requires the change to be **committed**: `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .dark-factory.yaml` exits 0 at the merge commit — otherwise a pathspec commit that skips the config leaves master on the `worktree` shape, and the next spec in this repo hits the same wall.

## Verification

`REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` throughout — it is a full 40-character SHA, which is exactly what the runner requires.

### Row 0 — the lane config (pre-landed and committed before approval; not a prompt)

- `grep -c '^workflow: direct$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
- `grep -c '^pr: false$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
- `grep -c '^defaultBranch: master$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
- `grep -c '^autoMerge: false$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
- `grep -cE '^(autoRelease: false|autoGeneratePrompts: true|validationPrompt: docs/dod\.md)$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 3
- `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .dark-factory.yaml` exits 0 at the merge commit — every grep above reads the working tree, not the commit

This shape is measured, not copied. On 2026-11-09 the same spec ran twice against PR #25: under `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true` the run failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/…: no such file or directory`; under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` all three prompts completed. `pr: true` is also rejected in combination with `workflow: direct`, so the two halves are one decision. The two older "completed siblings" carry `worktree` and predate the regression — do not cite them as the target shape.

### Container-executable — Row 1 (the `Makefile.docker` dispatch)

- `grep -c '^BUILD_TARGET' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1
- `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1
- `make -n build` prints a `docker build` recipe and no `hack/build-cluster.sh`
- `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` prints `hack/build-cluster.sh` and the composed `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe` line
- `make -n buca BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` exits non-zero naming the local-only targets
- `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` exits non-zero naming `VERSION`
- `grep -rn 'BUILD_TARGET' --exclude-dir=vendor . | grep -vE '(Makefile\.docker|README\.md|CHANGELOG\.md|hack/|specs/)'` returns 0 lines

### Container-executable — Row 2 (the runner files and the Dockerfile)

- `ls hack/` lists the five expected files — **not** `git ls-tree`, because verification runs pre-commit, when the new files are still untracked and absent from `HEAD`
- `bash -n hack/build-cluster.sh && bash -n hack/cluster-alias.sh && bash -n hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` — the copied runners parse
- `grep -c '\-mod=vendor' Dockerfile` returns 0
- `make precommit` — lint, format and vet clean
- `make test` — unit suites pass

### Container-executable — Row 3 (docs)

- `grep -c 'BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>' README.md` ≥ 1
- `grep -ci 'buca' README.md` ≥ 1
- `grep -c 'MIRROR_IMAGES' README.md` ≥ 1
- `awk '/^## /{s=$0} /cluster build/{print s}' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## Unreleased`

### Operator-executable (runs on the host after PR merge, spec verification ladder)

- `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh sun` — provisions the `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` secret; idempotent, creates no Job
- `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe-<timestamp>` — one real cluster build, Job name, node and both digests recorded
- `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe-<timestamp>` — the push landed, and equals the build log's digest
- `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack make build` then `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:v0.2.5` — the local arm still works

## Desired Behavior

1. **A build target selects the arm.** `BUILD_TARGET` defaults to `local`. With `local`, `make build` behaves exactly as it does today: it prepares the module cache, it runs `docker build` on this machine, and it tags `$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)`.
2. **Any other value routes to a cluster Job.** With `BUILD_TARGET` set to a cluster alias or kubectl context, `make build` prints the composed image reference, then renders the Job template and applies it through the copied runner, passing the repository URL and the push-secret name as literals. It waits for the Job and reports success or failure with the Job's own log lines.
3. **The cluster arm needs a caller-supplied tag.** The cluster arm refuses to run unless `VERSION` came from the command line or the environment. It refuses in particular when `VERSION` would resolve from `Makefile.docker`'s own `git describe` default, so a tag nobody chose can never be pushed. The refusal names the variable and happens before any Job is created.
4. **Both arms publish to one repository.** The cluster arm uses `$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)` — the same repository the local arm pushes and nuke's mirror copies, differing only in tag, and composed once so the two cannot drift.
5. **`upload`, `clean` and `buca` remain local-only.** Given a cluster `BUILD_TARGET` they are refused at parse time, by name, before any recipe runs.
6. **The cluster build works from a clone.** The image build resolves its Go dependencies in module mode, so a Job that clones the repo with no `vendor/` directory builds the same way a developer's checkout does. The local arm's `check-go-mod` preparation stays on the local branch only: the cluster arm builds a named ref, which need not be the local `HEAD`.
7. **The lane config is the shape that measured working on this repo.** `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `workflow: direct` with `pr: false` — the pair under which a cluster run completed all three prompts here, where `worktree` + `pr: true` failed at prompt-metadata write. `autoRelease: false` keeps the release manual, `autoGeneratePrompts: true` fires the generator, `autoMerge: false` leaves the merge to the reviewer, `defaultBranch: master` names the base and the `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md` gate stays. This change is **pre-landed and committed on the branch before the spec is approved**, so the lane is correct before the agent is ever asked to run.
8. **The documented build path matches reality.** The README's build section shows both arms, says `buca` stays local, and records why the cluster pushes Docker Hub while nuke's mirror produces the private copy. The CHANGELOG records the change.

## Constraints

- The local arm's command and its tag must not change.
- `VERSION`'s explicitness must be captured **before** `Makefile.docker`'s existing default assignment. After that `ifeq` block the variable's origin is `file` on every invocation, so a guard written below it never fires.
- `$(SERVICE)` may appear only in recipes or recursively-expanded (`=`) variables. `Makefile:3` includes `Makefile.docker` before `Makefile:5` assigns `SERVICE`, so a `:=` or an `ifeq` on it evaluates empty.
- The local-only refusal for `upload` / `clean` / `buca` is a `$(error …)` keyed on the goal list inside the non-local branch, not a recipe-level `exit 1`. A recipe-level refusal is invisible to `make -n`, so the AC could not observe it.
- The five `hack/` files are copied unmodified from `origin/master`: `hack/build-cluster.sh`, `hack/cluster-alias.sh` and `hack/build-job.yaml` from `agent-task-executor` (its Job spec carries `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, which `go-skeleton`'s does not), and `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` plus `hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl` from `go-skeleton`. Both repositories are public, so a `git clone --depth=1` from inside the container reaches them. `cluster-alias.sh` is required — the runner sources it and fails at that line without it.
- The Job template already passes `DOCKER_REGISTRY=docker.io` as a build argument, so the Dockerfile's base images resolve from the public registry inside the cluster rather than from the private mirror. Do not change that back to the mirror.
- `IMAGE`, `SERVICE`, the registry and the tag must each satisfy the runner's character whitelist; no value may carry a newline.
- `DOCKER_REGISTRY` keeps its `docker.io` default, so the composed reference stays `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`. No `CLUSTER_IMAGE` variable is needed: unlike the pilot, this repo already composes the `bborbe/`-prefixed path the cluster lane pushes.
- `IMAGE` and `TAG` are defined explicitly rather than left to the implementer to invent: `IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)` and `TAG = $(VERSION)`, both recursively expanded (`=`), because the runner consumes repository and tag as two separate variables and `$(SERVICE)` is unset at parse time. The dispatch passes both.
- `.dark-factory.yaml` keeps every other key verbatim — `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true`, `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`. The change is exactly two lines, `workflow` and `pr`; a rewrite that drops the validation gate is a regression.
- `README.md` gains the build section: it does not exist today (headings are `How It Works`, `Configuration`, `Observability`, `Task Contract`), so this spec makes it the in-repo home for the two-arm topology, the mirror coupling, and the two parse-time traps (`VERSION` defaulted before any guard can read its origin; `Makefile.docker` included before `SERVICE` is assigned). The spec dies after implementation; the README does not.
- No new scenario. The behaviour is reachable by checks on the rendered invocation plus one real cluster build.

## Assumptions

These must hold before the cluster AC can pass; none is created by this spec.

- The `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` dockerconfigjson secret exist in the target cluster, **and that credential covers the registry the arm pushes to**. It authenticates against Docker Hub, which is why the arm pushes `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`; a private-mirror push fails `401 Unauthorized` after a successful build.
- The repo is public, so the Job's anonymous `git fetch` succeeds; the init container carries no clone credential.
- `crane` is installed on the host running the ACs.
- `REF` exists in the local repository **and on `origin`**: the runner derives `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the local repository, and the Job's init container fetches the ref from the remote. A commit that exists only locally fails at the clone.
- The build pod can reach the Go module proxy.
- `kubectl` is configured for the target cluster through the alias files `hack/cluster-alias.sh` resolves.
- The prompt container can reach `github.com`, so the two copy-source repositories clone. If it cannot, fall back to copying the five files from a local sibling checkout (`~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor/hack/`, `~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton/hack/`).
- The draft PR carrying this approved spec is what triggers the watcher (`dark-factory-implement`, polled every 5 min), and the agent pushes its commits to that PR's branch. `master` is protected, so nothing lands there directly.

## Failure Modes

| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown cluster or context | The runner fails before applying anything and lists the accepted values | Re-run with a listed target; no Job exists to clean up |
| `VERSION` omitted on the cluster arm | Refusal before the Job is created, naming `VERSION` | Re-run passing `VERSION=<scratch-tag>` |
| `REF` is a short SHA, or is not in the local repository | The runner dies resolving `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` | `git fetch`, then re-run with the full 40-character SHA |
| `REF` exists locally but was never pushed | The clone init container fails: the ref does not exist on `origin` | Push the branch or commit, then re-run |
| The clone's commit epoch differs from the locally derived one | The build container refuses before `buildctl` runs and names both epochs | `git fetch`, then re-run |
| A Job with the derived name already exists in `build` | The runner refuses and names the existing Job rather than overwriting it | Delete the finished Job, then re-run |
| The runner is interrupted after `apply` | The Job keeps running in the cluster while the local invocation exits; the next run then hits the existing-Job refusal | Inspect `kubectlsun -n build get jobs`, read the pod's log, delete the Job once finished |
| The build pod cannot reach the module proxy | The Job fails; the runner prints the last 100 log lines and the Job name | Inspect the Job logs; the local arm is unaffected |
| The build pod is OOM-killed or throttled | The Job reports `failed`; the pod status carries `OOMKilled` or a CPU-throttling event | Raise the template's limits in the same change, or build locally for that one image |
| The registry throttles or rejects the push | The build fails at the push step with the registry's own error | Re-check the `build` namespace secret, then re-run |
| A caller-supplied `VERSION` names an already-released tag | No guard — the push replaces that tag irreversibly | Re-push the image from the released tag, then cut a new release |
| The built tag is not the one nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` references | The push lands in Docker Hub and the mirror copies the stale `CONSUMER_TAG` (`v0.1.0`), so the deployment does not move to the new image | Bump `CONSUMER_TAG` in `bborbe/nuke`'s `sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` — a separate deploy-side change, out of this spec's scope |
| The local arm regresses | `make build` fails or tags differently | Revert the arm; the local path is the regression gate |

## Security / Abuse Cases

- The runner substitutes caller-supplied values into a manifest and into embedded shell, so every value is checked against a character whitelist and rejected for embedded newlines before rendering. Do not add a value path that bypasses that check.
- The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not configurable inputs. The whitelist constrains the *shape* of a URL, not *which* repository is cloned and built with a mounted push credential; a configurable clone source on this build would let a caller point the credential-bearing Job at another repo.
- The build Job mounts a push credential from a `build`-namespace secret and runs with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. The credential is scoped to pushing an image; it grants nothing else.
- The build container runs as an unprivileged user with the sandbox profiles relaxed because rootless BuildKit requires it. That relaxation is deliberate and must not be copied to the clone init container.
- `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` reads a TeamVault credential into a `600` temp file and removes it on every exit path. It is never echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo. Do not add a logging path that prints the rendered secret.
- `VERSION` is caller-controlled and becomes an image tag and a Job name. The tag is whitelisted and the Job name is sanitized to a valid DNS name, truncated, and stripped of trailing separators.

## Suggested Decomposition

Prompts should be generated in this order — each row is a single prompt with a clear scope.

| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|

8	## Summary
9	
10	- This repo's image can currently be produced on one machine only: the Mac.
11	- Its sibling repos can also build their image inside a Kubernetes cluster, unattended, from any committed ref.
12	- Add that second build path here as an arm beside the existing local one, leaving the local command and tag as they are.
13	- The cluster arm builds a named commit as a Kubernetes Job and pushes the result to `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`, the repository nuke's mirror step copies into the private registry the deployment pulls from.
14	- Two supporting edits make the arm reachable: the image must build from a fresh clone with no `vendor/`, and the dark-factory lane config must stop using the shape that is known to lose commits.
15	
16	## Problem
17	
18	`sentry-alert-consumer` runs on nukeprod, and `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` mirrors `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(CONSUMER_TAG)` into `docker.prod.nuke.benjamin-borbe.de:443`. Every image that mirror copies is cut by hand on this Mac today: `Makefile.docker` carries only the local `docker build` path, and `hack/` does not exist. Nothing else can produce this image, so a release while the operator is away from this machine cannot happen.
19	
20	The arm is not a straight copy. Three properties of this repo make a naive paste fail at runtime rather than at review:
21	
22	- **`VERSION` is defaulted at parse time.** `Makefile.docker` opens with `ifeq ($(VERSION),) VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags …) endif`, so by the time any guard could read `$(origin VERSION)` the variable is `file` and an omitted tag silently resolves to the last released tag. A cluster arm that inherited that default would republish a released tag over itself, irreversibly.
23	- **`Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`.** `Makefile:3` is the include and `Makefile:5` is `SERVICE = sentry-alert-consumer`, so any parse-time use of `$(SERVICE)` inside `Makefile.docker` — an `ifeq`, a `:=` — evaluates empty and composes `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
24	- **The image build resolves dependencies from `vendor/`.** The Dockerfile runs `go build -mod=vendor`, `vendor/` is gitignored, and `origin/master` carries no `vendor/` directory. A Job that clones the repo has no `vendor/`, so the build fails before it starts.
25	
26	A fourth property only bites the lane rather than the build, and it was settled by measurement on this repo rather than by reading the docs. `.dark-factory.yaml` on `origin/master` carries `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true`, and a cluster run on exactly that config failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/001-spec-001-docs-build-section.md: no such file or directory` — the same signature recorded on `obsidian-redirector` PR #15. The identical spec run under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` completed all three prompts. So `direct` is the working shape here and `worktree` is the regression, whatever the two older "completed siblings" carry. `autoRelease: false` stays: it keeps the release manual, which this repo wants.
27	
28	## Goal
29	
30	`make build` on this repo produces the image locally exactly as it does today, and `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` produces it inside that cluster as a Kubernetes Job, pushing `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:<tag>` — the repository nuke's mirror step consumes. 31	
32	## Non-goals
33	
34	- Changing the local arm's command or its tag. Both stay as they are. The shared Dockerfile does move to module resolution, because the cluster arm cannot build from a clone otherwise; the local arm runs the same Dockerfile and is unaffected by how dependencies are fetched.
35	- Pushing to the private registry from the cluster. The `buildkit-push` credential authenticates against Docker Hub only; the private copy is produced by nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` step, not by this build.

119	7. **The lane config is the shape that measured working on this repo.** `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `workflow: direct` with `pr: false` — the pair under which a cluster run completed all three prompts here, where `worktree` + `pr: true` failed at prompt-metadata write. `autoRelease: false` keeps the release manual, `autoGeneratePrompts: true` fires the generator, `autoMerge: false` leaves the merge to the reviewer, `defaultBranch: master` names the base and the `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md` gate stays. This change is **pre-landed and committed on the branch before the spec is approved**, so the lane is correct before the agent is ever asked to run.
120	8. **The documented build path matches reality.** The README's build section shows both arms, says `buca` stays local, and records why the cluster pushes Docker Hub while nuke's mirror produces the private copy. The CHANGELOG records the change.
121	
122	## Constraints
123	
124	- The local arm's command and its tag must not change.
125	- `VERSION`'s explicitness must be captured **before** `Makefile.docker`'s existing default assignment. After that `ifeq` block the variable's origin is `file` on every invocation, so a guard written below it never fires.
126	- `$(SERVICE)` may appear only in recipes or recursively-expanded (`=`) variables. `Makefile:3` includes `Makefile.docker` before `Makefile:5` assigns `SERVICE`, so a `:=` or an `ifeq` on it evaluates empty.
127	- The local-only refusal for `upload` / `clean` / `buca` is a `$(error …)` keyed on the goal list inside the non-local branch, not a recipe-level `exit 1`. A recipe-level refusal is invisible to `make -n`, so the AC could not observe it.
128	- The five `hack/` files are copied unmodified from `origin/master`: `hack/build-cluster.sh`, `hack/cluster-alias.sh` and `hack/build-job.yaml` from `agent-task-executor` (its Job spec carries `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, which `go-skeleton`'s does not), and `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` plus `hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl` from `go-skeleton`. Both repositories are public, so a `git clone --depth=1` from inside the container reaches them. `cluster-alias.sh` is required — the runner sources it and fails at that line without it.
129	- The Job template already passes `DOCKER_REGISTRY=docker.io` as a build argument, so the Dockerfile's base images resolve from the public registry inside the cluster rather than from the private mirror. Do not change that back to the mirror.
130	- `IMAGE`, `SERVICE`, the registry and the tag must each satisfy the runner's character whitelist; no value may carry a newline.
131	- `DOCKER_REGISTRY` keeps its `docker.io` default, so the composed reference stays `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`. No `CLUSTER_IMAGE` variable is needed: unlike the pilot, this repo already composes the `bborbe/`-prefixed path the cluster lane pushes.
132	- `IMAGE` and `TAG` are defined explicitly rather than left to the implementer to invent: `IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)` and `TAG = $(VERSION)`, both recursively expanded (`=`), because the runner consumes repository and tag as two separate variables and `$(SERVICE)` is unset at parse time. The dispatch passes both.
133	- `.dark-factory.yaml` keeps every other key verbatim — `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true`, `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`. The change is exactly two lines, `workflow` and `pr`; a rewrite that drops the validation gate is a regression.
134	- `README.md` gains the build section: it does not exist today (headings are `How It Works`, `Configuration`, `Observability`, `Task Contract`), so this spec makes it the in-repo home for the two-arm topology, the mirror coupling, and the two parse-time traps (`VERSION` defaulted before any guard can read its origin; `Makefile.docker` included before `SERVICE` is assigned). The spec dies after implementation; the README does not.
135	- No new scenario. The behaviour is reachable by checks on the rendered invocation plus one real cluster build.
136	
137	## Assumptions
138	
139	These must hold before the cluster AC can pass; none is created by this spec.
140	
141	- The `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` dockerconfigjson secret exist in the target cluster, **and that credential covers the registry the arm pushes to**. It authenticates against Docker Hub, which is why the arm pushes `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`; a private-mirror push fails `401 Unauthorized` after a successful build.
142	- The repo is public, so the Job's anonymous `git fetch` succeeds; the init container carries no clone credential.
143	- `crane` is installed on the host running the ACs.
144	- `REF` exists in the local repository **and on `origin`**: the runner derives `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the local repository, and the Job's init container fetches the ref from the remote. A commit that exists only locally fails at the clone.
145	- The build pod can reach the Go module proxy.
146	- `kubectl` is configured for the target cluster through the alias files `hack/cluster-alias.sh` resolves.
147	- The prompt container can reach `github.com`, so the two copy-source repositories clone. If it cannot, fall back to copying the five files from a local sibling checkout (`~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor/hack/`, `~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton/hack/`).
148	- The draft PR carrying this approved spec is what triggers the watcher (`dark-factory-implement`, polled every 5 min), and the agent pushes its commits to that PR's branch. `master` is protected, so nothing lands there directly.
149	
150	## Failure Modes
151	
152	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
153	|---|---|---|
154	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown cluster or context | The runner fails before applying anything and lists the accepted values | Re-run with a listed target; no Job exists to clean up |
155	| `VERSION` omitted on the cluster arm | Refusal before the Job is created, naming `VERSION` | Re-run passing `VERSION=<scratch-tag>` |
156	| `REF` is a short SHA, or is not in the local repository | The runner dies resolving `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` | `git fetch`, then re-run with the full 40-character SHA |
157	| `REF` exists locally but was never pushed | The clone init container fails: the ref does not exist on `origin` | Push the branch or commit, then re-run |
158	| The clone's commit epoch differs from the locally derived one | The build container refuses before `buildctl` runs and names both epochs | `git fetch`, then re-run |
159	| A Job with the derived name already exists in `build` | The runner refuses and names the existing Job rather than overwriting it | Delete the finished Job, then re-run |
160	| The runner is interrupted after `apply` | The Job keeps running in the cluster while the local invocation exits; the next run then hits the existing-Job refusal | Inspect `kubectlsun -n build get jobs`, read the pod's log, delete the Job once finished |
161	| The build pod cannot reach the module proxy | The Job fails; the runner prints the last 100 log lines and the Job name | Inspect the Job logs; the local arm is unaffected |
162	| The build pod is OOM-killed or throttled | The Job reports `failed`; the pod status carries `OOMKilled` or a CPU-throttling event | Raise the template's limits in the same change, or build locally for that one image |
163	| The registry throttles or rejects the push | The build fails at the push step with the registry's own error | Re-check the `build` namespace secret, then re-run |
164	| A caller-supplied `VERSION` names an already-released tag | No guard — the push replaces that tag irreversibly | Re-push the image from the released tag, then cut a new release |
165	| The built tag is not the one nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` references | The push lands in Docker Hub and the mirror copies the stale `CONSUMER_TAG` (`v0.1.0`), so the deployment does not move to the new image | Bump `CONSUMER_TAG` in `bborbe/nuke`'s `sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` — a separate deploy-side change, out of this spec's scope |
166	| The local arm regresses | `make build` fails or tags differently | Revert the arm; the local path is the regression gate |
167	
168	## Security / Abuse Cases
169	
170	- The runner substitutes caller-supplied values into a manifest and into embedded shell, so every value is checked against a character whitelist and rejected for embedded newlines before rendering. Do not add a value path that bypasses that check.
171	- The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not configurable inputs. The whitelist constrains the *shape* of a URL, not *which* repository is cloned and built with a mounted push credential; a configurable clone source on this build would let a caller point the credential-bearing Job at another repo.
172	- The build Job mounts a push credential from a `build`-namespace secret and runs with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. The credential is scoped to pushing an image; it grants nothing else.
173	- The build container runs as an unprivileged user with the sandbox profiles relaxed because rootless BuildKit requires it. That relaxation is deliberate and must not be copied to the clone init container.
174	- `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` reads a TeamVault credential into a `600` temp file and removes it on every exit path. It is never echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo. Do not add a logging path that prints the rendered secret.
175	- `VERSION` is caller-controlled and becomes an image tag and a Job name. The tag is whitelisted and the Job name is sanitized to a valid DNS name, truncated, and stripped of trailing separators.
176	
177	## Suggested Decomposition
178	
179	Prompts should be generated in this order — each row is a single prompt with a clear scope.
180	
181	| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
182	|---|---|---|---|---|
183	| 0 | **Not a prompt.** `.dark-factory.yaml` → `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` (the measured-working shape), keeping `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true` and `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`, plus `defaultBranch: master` and `autoMerge: false`. Pre-landed and **committed** on the branch before approval. Satisfies AC 8's `.dark-factory.yaml` clause, so no prompt re-implements it. | 7 | 8 (config clause only) | — |
184	| 1 | The `Makefile.docker` dispatch: the `BUILD_TARGET` split, `IMAGE`/`TAG`, the explicitness capture before the default, the composed-reference echo, and local-only `upload`/`clean`/`buca` | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | 1, 3, 4, 6 | row 0 |
185	| 2 | The build path itself: the five `hack/` files and the module-mode image build | 2, 6 | 2, 5, 7 | prompt 1 (the dispatch calls the runner) |
186	| 3 | Docs: the README build section and the CHANGELOG bullet | 8 | 8 | — |
187	
188	Rationale: row 0 is pre-landed rather than prompted because the lane config must be correct **before** the agent is asked to run — a prompt that fixes the config it is itself running under is a chicken-and-egg. With it in place, prompt 1 establishes the dispatch, prompt 2 supplies the runner it calls and the Dockerfile change that lets it work from a clone, and prompt 3 is independent and touches no build logic.
189	
190	## Do-Nothing Option
191	
192	Leaving this repo without a cluster arm keeps one nukeprod watcher's image tied to the Mac. Every rebuild, every release cut while the operator is away from this machine, and every future unattended pipeline needs a human at the keyboard for this one repo — while its siblings build themselves. The cost is not the one build; it is that the automation has a hole shaped exactly like the repo nobody is watching.
193

1	# sentry-alert-consumer
2	
3	Consumes the `{branch}-raw-sentry-alert-input` Kafka topic and publishes one
4	`CreateTaskCommand` per derived (issue-key, date) so the `sentry-analyzer-agent`
5	can classify each alert — replacing the `sentry-collector-agent`'s token-REST
6	fan-out as the trigger of the Sentry pipeline.
7	
8	The consumer is the **Kafka-native trigger** front of the Sentry pipeline. It
9	reads the complete alert stream (including alerts Sentry never accepted —
10	spike-protected or over-quota, which the API can never show), derives an issue
11	identity from each raw Sentry envelope, and emits one "Analyze Sentry issue
12	<KEY> - <date>" task into the Personal vault. Sentry API access continues only
13	as per-task enrichment inside the analyzer (`sentry-read.sh`), never as the
14	trigger.
15	
16	## How It Works
17	
18	For each message on the alert topic:
19	
20	1. **Parse the tee record** — JSON `{body, project, received_at, outcome}` as
21	   published by `sentry-proxy`'s Kafka tee (spec 001). `body` is the raw Sentry
22	   envelope; `outcome` is `forwarded` / `rejected` / `upstream_error`.
23	2. **Gate on the outcome** — only a `forwarded` event was stored by Sentry, so
24	   only it has an issue to analyse. A `rejected` or `upstream_error` record is
25	   counted (`skipped_non_forwarded`) and skipped before any parsing: it has no
26	   issue identity, so its key would be the per-event `event-<event_id>`, which
27	   nothing can dedup — one analyzer task per rejected event. The rejection rate
28	   stays observable through `events_total{outcome="rejected"}`.
29	3. **Parse the envelope** — extract `event_id` and the event payload
30	   (exception, message). Best-effort: a missing or malformed event payload
31	   degrades to the envelope header's `event_id`, never dropping the record.
32	4. **Derive the issue** — grouping per the consumer contract:
33	   - dedup key: `event_id`
34	   - issue key: first exception `type`+`value`+`module` → `message` hash →
35	     `event_id` (per-event fallback) → body hash (unparseable-envelope fallback)
36	   - title: exception value → message → "(no message)"
37	   - date: the event timestamp's UTC calendar date, falling back to
38	     `received_at`
39	5. **Enrich forwarded events** — only for `outcome: forwarded`, resolve the
40	   event's numeric Sentry issue id via
41	   `GET {SENTRY_URL}/api/0/organizations/{SENTRY_ORG}/eventids/{event_id}/`
42	   (scope `org:read`) and emit it as `short_id` + `issue_url`, so the analyzer
43	   can run its live-state fetch (`sentry-read.sh`, which requires `^[0-9]+$`).
44	   A rejected event was never stored by Sentry, so its lookup is a guaranteed
45	   404 that only burns quota — it is skipped. On a **successful** lookup the
46	   issue key itself is replaced by the numeric id, so
47	   `UUID5("kafka:" + issue-key + ":" + date)` collapses a same-day repeat of one
48	   issue into a single task. A miss (forwarded but dropped by quota) or any
49	   lookup failure keeps the derived key and still publishes the task:
50	   enrichment never drops an alert. The `event-<event_id>` and body-hash
51	   fallbacks therefore remain only for those miss and failure paths — they are
52	   not dead code.
53	6. **Publish one `CreateTaskCommand`** per (issue-key, date). Task identity is
54	   `UUID5("kafka:" + issue-key + ":" + date)` over the same namespace as the
55	   collector's `/create-tasks`, so the two identity spaces never collide and
56	   controller dedup makes re-emits (including full-topic replays after a
57	   restart) a no-op.
58	
59	The emitted task contract is preserved from `cmd/create-tasks`:
60	`task_type: sentry-issue-analyzer`, `assignee: sentry-analyzer-agent`, `stage`
61	derived from the project slug (`nuke-prod`→prod, `nuke-dev`→dev), `status:
62	in_progress`, Personal-vault target.
63	
64	## Configuration
65	
66	| Env | Default | Purpose |
67	|-----|---------|---------|
68	| `SENTRY_API_TOKEN` | *(empty)* | Sentry API token (scope `org:read`) for event→issue enrichment; empty disables enrichment — the binary runs and tasks keep the derived key |
69	| `SENTRY_URL` | `https://bborbe.sentry.io` | Sentry base URL for the enrichment lookup |
70	| `SENTRY_ORG` | `bborbe` | Sentry organization slug for the enrichment lookup |
71	
72	## Observability
73	
74	- `sentry_alert_consumer_messages_total{result}` — processed / parse_error /
75	  envelope_error / payload_parse_error / build_error / publish_error /
76	  enrich_error / enrich_retry_exhausted / enrich_miss / skipped_heartbeat /
77	  skipped_non_forwarded
78	- `sentry_alert_consumer_events_total{outcome}` — forwarded / rejected /
79	  upstream_error. Every outcome is counted here, including the ones that no
80	  longer publish a task, so the rejection rate stays alertable on its own.
81	- `sentry_alert_consumer_published_total{status}` — create / error
82	- `sentry_alert_consumer_last_event_timestamp` — Unix seconds of the last
83	  processed event; a silence alert thresholds on this (empty-topic vs
84	  broken-consumer detection is a separate alerting concern)
85	
86	## Task Contract
87	
88	See the task "Analyse Sentry Alerts Directly From the Kafka Topic" § Consumer
89	Contract for the full contract, including the silence-window and
90	enrichment-only Sentry API decisions.
91

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
4	
5	Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).
6	
7	## Unreleased
8	
9	- chore: restate the do-not-merge contract in the gate workflow
10	- chore: update Go to 1.27.3 and github.com/IBM/sarama to v1.61.1, github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.114.0, github.com/bborbe/cqrs to v0.6.12, github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.6.3, github.com/bborbe/http to v1.26.30, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.28.5, github.com/bborbe/log to v1.7.5, github.com/bborbe/run to v1.11.2, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.5, github.com/bborbe/service to v1.11.1, github.com/bborbe/time to v1.27.18, github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 to v2.33.1, github.com/onsi/gomega to v1.44.0, github.com/prometheus/client_golang to v1.25.0
11	
12	- chore(dark-factory): worktree workflow with PR delivery
13	
14	## v0.2.5
15	
16	- fix: re-key an enriched record on the numeric Sentry issue id. `enrichIssue`
17	  wrote back `NumericID` and `IssueURL` but never `Key`, so the published
18	  `CreateTaskCommand` stayed keyed on the envelope-derived identity — a
19	  per-event `event-<event_id>` for a forwarded event carrying no
20	  exception/message, which nothing can dedup. Two events of one issue on the
21	  same day therefore produced two analyzer tasks even though the lookup had
22	  resolved both to the same issue (measured 2026-10-19 on prod: 3 of 16
23	  forwarded records). The re-key covers every successful enrichment, so the
24	  32-hex derived hashes collapse too.
25	
26	## v0.2.4
27	
28	- fix: publish an analyzer task only for `forwarded` records. A `rejected` or
29	  `upstream_error` event was never stored by Sentry, so it has no issue identity
30	  and `deriveIssueKey` falls back to the per-event `event-<event_id>` key, which
31	  nothing can dedup — one task per rejected event, measured 2026-10-18 on dev at
32	  73 of 74 processed records, against a ~12/day baseline. Non-forwarded records
33	  are now counted as `messages_total{result="skipped_non_forwarded"}` and skipped
34	  before parsing; `events_total{outcome}` still counts every outcome, so the
35	  rejection rate stays alertable on its own.
36	
37	## v0.2.3
38	
39	- fix: report `eventAge` on the `enriched` line as the offset to the **first lookup attempt** rather than the offset to the log line. The field is read as evidence that a lookup happened inside Sentry's ingest-indexing window, but `time.Since(eventTime)` was evaluated *after* `IssueRef` returned, so it folded the dedicated 404 schedule's +1/+3/+6/+10 s waits into the number: a fresh event that retried before succeeding read as an old one, which is precisely the distinction the field exists to make. Observed on dev 2026-10-14 — an event logged `eventAge=7.615s` whose actual first lookup ran at +0.632 s, leaving the parent task's `eventAge < 3 s` criterion readable only by deriving the offset from raw log timestamps. The clock is now injected (`libtime.CurrentDateTimeGetter`) rather than read from `time.Now()`, so the specs assert the logged value exactly, and they are pinned to fail against the previous expression.
40	
41	## v0.2.2
42	
43	- fix: count a present-but-unparseable envelope event payload as `payload_parse_error` and log it with the event_id, instead of dropping it silently — `parseEventPayload` returned nil on a JSON unmarshal failure with no log and no metric, so the record degraded to the header/body-hash identity and was still counted as `processed`; that silence is what let the bare-array exception (v0.1.6) and bare-string message (PR #11) defects run undetected for weeks. The label is pre-initialised so `rate()` has a series from startup, and it stays distinct from `parse_error`, which is a Kafka *record* that did not parse. A payload that is absent entirely is not counted — only one that was present and unreadable.
44	
45	## v0.2.1
46	
47	- fix: retry a 404 from the eventids lookup on a dedicated schedule (+1/+3/+6/+10 s, 4 extra lookups) when the event is still inside Sentry's ingest-indexing window, so an event Sentry has stored but not yet indexed is enriched instead of silently keeping its derived key. A 404 was treated as permanent, so every lookup landing within a few seconds of the event's creation produced a derived-key task and an `unanalyzable` verdict — reproduced at +2.58 s and +0.91 s after `date_created`, and measured on the prod consumer as 0 successes in 61 attempts. The schedule is deliberately separate from the error-retry budget (which stays at 3 attempts / 2 s and still does not retry a 404): the error budget answers "is Sentry having a moment?", the schedule answers "has Sentry finished indexing this event yet?". It is skipped for events older than 30 s, because a record replayed from the topic has a real miss and holding a partition 10 s per record would stall a 45-miss replay burst for minutes. The miss is now counted as `enrich_miss` (pre-initialised, so `rate()` has a series from startup) rather than logged at V(2) only — the counter is what makes a return of this failure visible instead of silent.
48	- fix: bump `osv-scanner` to v2.6.0 and `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 so the Linux vulnerability gates stop failing. v2.3.1 pins `golang.org/x/tools` v0.38.0, whose SSA builder aborts with `unexpected expr: *ast.KeyValueExpr` on the promoted-field composite-literal key Go 1.27 permits in the Linux stdlib, so a repo on the old pin passes locally on darwin and fails only in Linux CI. `x/net` v0.58.0 carries `GO-2026-6603/6610/6611/6612/6617`, which fail both `vulncheck` and `trivy`.
49

DIRS += $(shell find */* -maxdepth 0 -name Makefile -exec dirname "{}" \;)

# BUILD_TARGET selects where `make build` runs. `local` (the default) uses the
# local Docker daemon; any other value names a cluster alias (sun / nukedev /
# nukeprod) and builds inside that cluster as a Job rendered from
# hack/build-job.yaml.
BUILD_TARGET ?= local
# The build namespace is fixed at `build` by the dispatcher-consumed
# hack/build-job.yaml, so there is no BUILD_NAMESPACE knob here.
BUILD_TIMEOUT ?= 3600
BUILD_REPO_URL ?= https://github.com/$(IMAGE).git
BUILD_DOCKERFILE ?= Dockerfile
BUILD_PUSH_SECRET ?= buildkit-push

.PHONY: build
build: check-version-tag
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	@if [ -z "$(VERSION)" ]; then echo "ERROR: no VERSION set and no git tag found — set VERSION=vX.Y.Z or create a tag" >&2; exit 1; fi
	DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 \
	docker build \
	--pull \
	--no-cache \
	--rm=true \
	--platform=linux/amd64 \
	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_VERSION=$$(git describe --tags --always --dirty) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
	-t $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) \
	-f Dockerfile .
else
# The cluster arm publishes at VERSION and cannot use check-version-tag: that
# guard compares the local HEAD's tag, which is meaningless when the Job clones
# an arbitrary REF. It would also silently pass a VERSION that is merely the
# Makefile's default — `git describe --tags $(git rev-list --tags --max-count=1)`
# resolves to the newest release tag, so a bare `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun`
# would push over that released image. Require the caller to name the tag:
#   make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>
	@if [ "$(origin VERSION)" = "file" ] && [ -z "$(ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION)" ]; then \
		echo "ERROR: the cluster arm needs an explicit VERSION." >&2; \
		echo "  VERSION was defaulted to $(VERSION), which is the newest release tag." >&2; \
		echo "  Building over it would replace a released image." >&2; \
		echo "  Pass VERSION=<scratch-tag>, or set ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION=1 to build the default deliberately." >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi
	BUILD_TARGET='$(BUILD_TARGET)' \
	REPO_URL='$(BUILD_REPO_URL)' \
	REF='$(REF)' \
	TAG='$(VERSION)' \
	DOCKERFILE='$(BUILD_DOCKERFILE)' \
	IMAGE='$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE)' \
	DOCKER_REGISTRY='$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)' \
	PUSH='true' \
	PUSH_SECRET='$(BUILD_PUSH_SECRET)' \
	TIMEOUT='$(BUILD_TIMEOUT)' \
	hack/build-cluster.sh
endif

.PHONY: check-version-tag
check-version-tag:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	@if [ -n "$(ALLOW_UNTAGGED_BUILD)" ]; then \
		echo "ALLOW_UNTAGGED_BUILD set — skipping version/tag check"; \
	else \
		head_tag=$$(git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2>/dev/null); \
		if [ "$$head_tag" != "$(VERSION)" ]; then \
			echo "ERROR: refusing to build $(VERSION) from this tree." >&2; \
			echo "  HEAD is at tag: $${head_tag:-<untagged>}" >&2; \
			echo "  building as:    $(VERSION)" >&2; \
			echo "  An image stamped vX.Y.Z must be built from the vX.Y.Z tag." >&2; \
			echo "  Fix: git checkout $(VERSION)   (or set ALLOW_UNTAGGED_BUILD=1 for a scratch build)" >&2; \
			exit 1; \
		fi; \
	fi
endif

# No host-side `go mod vendor`: the image builds in module mode and downloads its
# own dependencies (see Dockerfile). Vendoring on the host would leave a vendor/
# that `COPY . .` picks up, and Go then selects vendor mode automatically — which
# is exactly the local/cluster divergence this repo no longer has.

.PHONY: upload
upload:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	docker push $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION)
else
	@echo "upload: nothing to do — the cluster arm already pushed the image"
endif

.PHONY: clean
clean:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	docker rmi $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) || true
	docker image prune -f || true
	docker builder prune --all -f || true
	rm -rf vendor
else
	@echo "clean: nothing to do — the cluster arm leaves nothing on this host"
endif

.PHONY: apply
apply:
	@for i in $(DIRS); do \
		cd $$i; \
		echo "apply $${i}"; \
		make apply; \
		cd ..; \
	done

# Operator-run publish. buca is the local path: with BUILD_TARGET set the image
# is pushed at $(VERSION) and nothing is deployed, so run buca with the default
# local arm only.
.PHONY: buca
buca: build upload clean apply
