DIRS += $(shell find */* -maxdepth 0 -name Makefile -exec dirname "{}" \;)

# BUILD_TARGET selects where `make build` runs. `local` (the default) uses the
# local Docker daemon; any other value must name a kubectl context and builds
# inside that cluster as a Job rendered from hack/build-job.yaml.
BUILD_TARGET ?= local
BUILD_NAMESPACE ?= build
BUILD_TIMEOUT ?= 3600
BUILD_REPO_URL ?= https://github.com/$(SERVICE).git
BUILD_DOCKERFILE ?= Dockerfile
BUILD_PUSH_SECRET ?= buildkit-push

# Build clock, pinned to the built commit instead of the wall clock so that two
# builds of the same commit can produce the same image. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is
# consumed by BuildKit for timestamp clamping; BUILD_DATE is the value the
# Dockerfile bakes into the image labels.
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH ?= $(shell git log -1 --format=%ct)
BUILD_DATE ?= $(shell git log -1 --format=%cI)

# The local build goes through buildx so the exporter can rewrite layer
# timestamps from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. `docker build` pins the image config clock
# but not the layer tars, so two builds of one commit still differed.
#   - `type=docker` loads the result into the local Docker store (as `--load`
#     does), so `make upload` and `docker run` keep working.
#   - `unpack=false` is required: `rewrite-timestamp` conflicts with `unpack`.
#   - provenance/sbom are disabled because their attestation manifests carry
#     their own build timestamps, which would make the image ID differ again.
# The active builder must be a `docker`-driver builder (`docker buildx ls`, the
# `*` row); a `docker-container` builder is a separate build cache and is not
# what this recipe was measured against.

.PHONY: build
build:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	docker buildx build \
	--platform=linux/amd64 \
	--provenance=false \
	--sbom=false \
	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
	--build-arg BRANCH=$(BRANCH) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_VERSION=$$(git describe --tags --always --dirty) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$(BUILD_DATE) \
	--build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) \
	-t $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(SERVICE):$(BRANCH) \
	-f Dockerfile . \
	--output type=docker,rewrite-timestamp=true,unpack=false
else
# The cluster arm publishes at VERSION rather than BRANCH. In a detached worktree —
# which is what a release build uses — `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints the
# literal string `HEAD`, so the image landed at `:HEAD` instead of at the tag it was
# told to build, and the tag itself stayed empty.
#
# VERSION deliberately has no default. `hack/build-cluster.sh` already dies on an
# empty TAG, so an unset VERSION is a loud failure; any default would instead publish
# a tag the checked-out tree does not correspond to. Pass it explicitly:
#   make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>
	BUILD_TARGET='$(BUILD_TARGET)' \
	NAMESPACE='$(BUILD_NAMESPACE)' \
	REPO_URL='$(BUILD_REPO_URL)' \
	REF='$(REF)' \
	TAG='$(VERSION)' \
	DOCKERFILE='$(BUILD_DOCKERFILE)' \
	IMAGE='$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(SERVICE)' \
	PUSH='true' \
	PUSH_SECRET='$(BUILD_PUSH_SECRET)' \
	TIMEOUT='$(BUILD_TIMEOUT)' \
	hack/build-cluster.sh
endif

# A remote target pushes from inside the cluster and never loads the image on
# this machine, so there is nothing here to push and nothing to remove. Guard
# both, or `make buca BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` fails at the push step after a
# build that actually succeeded.
.PHONY: upload
upload:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	docker push $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(SERVICE):$(BRANCH)
endif

.PHONY: clean
clean:
ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
	docker rmi $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/$(SERVICE):$(BRANCH) || true
	docker builder prune --max-used-space 21474836480 -f || true
endif

.PHONY: apply
apply:
	@for i in $(DIRS); do \
		cd $$i; \
		echo "apply $${i}"; \
		make apply; \
		cd ..; \
	done

.PHONY: buca
buca: build upload clean apply

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Renders hack/build-job.yaml and runs it in the target cluster.
3	#
4	# Called from `make build BUILD_TARGET=<sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>`
5	# (Makefile.docker) with
6	# BUILD_TARGET, NAMESPACE, REPO_URL, REF, TAG, DOCKERFILE, IMAGE, PUSH,
7	# PUSH_SECRET and TIMEOUT in the environment. Not intended to be run by hand.
8	set -euo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-job.yaml}"
12	
13	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
14	PUSH="${PUSH:-true}"
15	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3600}"
16	DOCKERFILE="${DOCKERFILE:-Dockerfile}"
17	DOCKER_REGISTRY="${DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
18	
19	die() {
20		echo "build-cluster: $*" >&2
21		exit 1
22	}
23	
24	require() {
25		local name="$1"
26		[ -n "${!name:-}" ] || die "${name} is required; pass it on the make command line"
27	}
28	
29	# BUILD_TARGET is resolved to a kubeconfig file and context by cluster-alias.sh,
30	# which also defines the kc() helper every kubectl call goes through.
31	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
32	
33	# The equivalent invocation for messages the operator has to retype.
34	KUBE_HINT="kubectl --context ${KUBE_CONTEXT}"
35	[ -z "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] || KUBE_HINT="KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG_PATH} ${KUBE_HINT}"
36	
37	require BUILD_TARGET
38	require REPO_URL
39	require REF
40	require TAG
41	require IMAGE
42	require PUSH_SECRET
43	
44	# Values are substituted into the manifest with sed and land in shell scripts
45	# inside it, so each one is restricted to a whitelist before rendering. A value
46	# outside the whitelist is rejected, never escaped.
47	printf '%s' "${REF}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
48		die "REF '${REF}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
49	printf '%s' "${TAG}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
50		die "TAG '${TAG}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
51	printf '%s' "${IMAGE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
52		die "IMAGE '${IMAGE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
53	printf '%s' "${REPO_URL}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]+$' ||
54		die "REPO_URL '${REPO_URL}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]"
55	printf '%s' "${DOCKERFILE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
56		die "DOCKERFILE '${DOCKERFILE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
57	printf '%s' "${PUSH_SECRET}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
58		die "PUSH_SECRET '${PUSH_SECRET}' is not a valid Kubernetes secret name"
59	printf '%s' "${DOCKER_REGISTRY}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
60		die "DOCKER_REGISTRY '${DOCKER_REGISTRY}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
61	printf '%s' "${TIMEOUT}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
62		die "TIMEOUT '${TIMEOUT}' is not a number of seconds"
63	printf '%s' "${NAMESPACE}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
64		die "NAMESPACE '${NAMESPACE}' is not a valid Kubernetes namespace name"
65	case "${PUSH}" in
66	true | false) ;;
67	*) die "PUSH '${PUSH}' must be true or false" ;;
68	esac
69	
70	# `grep -qE '^...$'` matches when ANY line matches, so a value carrying a newline
71	# passes the whitelist on its first line and its remaining lines are injected
72	# verbatim by sed into the YAML and the embedded `sh -c` script. Reject embedded
73	# newlines for every value before rendering.
74	for _var in REF TAG IMAGE REPO_URL DOCKERFILE PUSH_SECRET DOCKER_REGISTRY TIMEOUT NAMESPACE; do
75		case "${!_var}" in
76		*$'\n'*) die "${_var} contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
77		esac
78	done
79	
80	if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] && [ ! -f "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
81		die "BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}' needs the kubeconfig ${KUBECONFIG_PATH}, which does not exist"
82	fi
83	
84	# The accepted targets are the contexts the resolved kubeconfig knows about, so
85	# an unknown target fails here with the list instead of at apply time. The
86	# aliases are listed too: they are valid inputs without being contexts.
87	contexts="$(kc config get-contexts -o name 2>/dev/null || true)"
88	printf '%s\n' "${contexts}" | grep -qxF "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" ||
89		die "unknown BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod $(printf '%s' "${contexts}" | tr '\n' ' ')"
90	
91	# The build clock is the built commit's timestamp. It is rendered literally so
92	# the Job states the epoch it will use; the init container re-derives it from
93	# the cloned commit and the build container refuses to run on a mismatch.
94	if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
95		SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH="$(git log -1 --format=%ct "${REF}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
96	fi
97	printf '%s' "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
98		die "cannot resolve REF '${REF}' to a commit in the local repository; run git fetch and retry"
99	# SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is the one substituted value the loop above cannot cover: it
100	# is derived here, after that loop runs, and is spliced into both the YAML and
101	# the embedded `sh -c` script just like the rest.
102	case "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" in
103	*$'\n'*) die "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
104	esac
105	
106	JOB_NAME="build-$(printf '%s' "${TAG}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -e 's/[^a-z0-9.-]/-/g')"
107	JOB_NAME="${JOB_NAME:0:63}"
108	# Truncation can leave a trailing '.' or '-', which is not a valid DNS-1123 name.
109	JOB_NAME="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME}" | sed -e 's/[-.]*$//')"
110	
111	rendered="$(mktemp)"
112	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}"' EXIT
113	
114	sed \
115		-e "s|__JOB_NAME__|${JOB_NAME}|g" \
116		-e "s|__REPO_URL__|${REPO_URL}|g" \
117		-e "s|__REF__|${REF}|g" \
118		-e "s|__TAG__|${TAG}|g" \
119		-e "s|__DOCKERFILE__|${DOCKERFILE}|g" \
120		-e "s|__IMAGE__|${IMAGE}|g" \
121		-e "s|__PUSH__|${PUSH}|g" \
122		-e "s|__PUSH_SECRET__|${PUSH_SECRET}|g" \
123		-e "s|__DEADLINE_SECONDS__|${TIMEOUT}|g" \
124		-e "s|__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__|${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}|g" \
125		-e "s|__DOCKER_REGISTRY__|${DOCKER_REGISTRY}|g" \
126		-e "s|__NAMESPACE__|${NAMESPACE}|g" \
127		"${TEMPLATE}" >"${rendered}"
128	
129	# The rendered manifest, not the environment, decides the namespace. A template
130	# may hardcode `namespace:` instead of carrying the token, and polling the
131	# requested NAMESPACE would then watch a namespace the Job was never created in
132	# until the deadline expired.
133	#
134	# Anchored to the metadata block and stopped at the first match: an unanchored
135	# pattern would take a nested `namespace:` (a RoleBinding, a second document) as
136	# metadata, and `sed | head -1` can die on SIGPIPE once a second match exists.
137	rendered_namespace="$(awk '
138		/^metadata:/ { in_meta = 1; next }
139		in_meta && /^[^[:space:]]/ { exit }
140		in_meta && /^[[:space:]]*namespace:/ {
141			sub(/^[[:space:]]*namespace:[[:space:]]*/, "")
142			print
143			exit
144		}
145	' "${rendered}")"
146	printf '%s' "${rendered_namespace}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
147		die "rendered manifest has no valid metadata.namespace (got '${rendered_namespace}')"
148	NAMESPACE="${rendered_namespace}"
149	
150	# A kubectl failure must not read as "no such Job": an RBAC denial, a missing
151	# namespace and a bad context otherwise look exactly like an absent object, and
152	# the script would go on to apply.
153	#
154	# stdout is the existence signal and stderr is the diagnostic, kept apart: a
155	# warning on a *successful* `get` — kubectl prints a client/server version-skew
156	# warning on every server-contacting command — must not be read as an existing
157	# Job, or a healthy cluster refuses every build with a false message.
158	kubectl_err="$(mktemp)"
159	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}" "${kubectl_err}"' EXIT
160	if existing="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" --ignore-not-found -o name 2>"${kubectl_err}")"; then
161		[ -z "${existing}" ] || die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} already exists; delete it with: ${KUBE_HINT} -n ${NAMESPACE} delete job ${JOB_NAME}"
162	else
163		die "cannot read job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}: $(cat "${kubectl_err}")"
164	fi
165	rm -f "${kubectl_err}"
166	
167	if ! kc apply -f "${rendered}"; then
168		echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} was not accepted; events:" >&2
169		kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get events \
170			--field-selector "involvedObject.name=${JOB_NAME}" \
171			--sort-by=.lastTimestamp >&2 || true
172		die "could not create job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}"
173	fi
174	
175	# 10# forces base 10: TIMEOUT is validated as digits only, but a value with a
176	# leading zero (0800) would otherwise be parsed as octal and abort the arithmetic.
177	deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 10#${TIMEOUT} + 120 ))
178	outcome=""
179	while [ -z "${outcome}" ]; do
180		succeeded="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
181		failed="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
182		if [ "${succeeded:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
183			outcome=succeeded
184		elif [ "${failed:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
185			outcome=failed
186		elif [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "${deadline}" ]; then
187			outcome=timeout
188		else
189			sleep 5
190		fi
191	done
192	
193	logs() {
194		kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" logs \
195			-l "job-name=${JOB_NAME}" --all-containers --prefix "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
196	}
197	
198	if [ "${outcome}" = succeeded ]; then
199		logs --tail=-1 | grep -E 'pushing manifest for|containerimage\.digest' || true
200		echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} succeeded"
201		exit 0
202	fi
203	
204	echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} ${outcome}; last log lines:" >&2
205	logs --tail=100 >&2
206	if [ "${outcome}" = timeout ]; then
207		die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} did not finish within ${TIMEOUT}s (+120s grace)"
208	fi
209	die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} failed"
210

1	# Parameterized BuildKit build Job.
2	#
3	# Rendered and applied by the release-to-image dispatcher when this repo is
4	# released, and by `hack/build-cluster.sh` when `make build` runs with a
5	# BUILD_TARGET other than `local`. The default local arm does not use it:
6	# `make build` with no BUILD_TARGET still builds with plain `docker build`.
7	#
8	# This file lives outside k8s/ on purpose: everything under k8s/ is deploy
9	# state reached through `make apply`, so a template kept there would be adopted
10	# as such.
11	#
12	# Template tokens:
13	#   __JOB_NAME__           Job name, derived from __TAG__ and sanitized for DNS
14	#   __REPO_URL__           git URL to clone
15	#   __REF__                git ref (branch, tag or commit) to build
16	#   __TAG__                image tag to push
17	#   __DOCKERFILE__         Dockerfile path inside the repository
18	#   __IMAGE__              target image repository, without tag
19	#   __PUSH__               "true" to push the built image
20	#   __PUSH_SECRET__        name of the dockerconfigjson secret to mount
21	#   __DEADLINE_SECONDS__   Job deadline in seconds
22	#   __SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__  commit timestamp, decimal seconds
23	#
24	# Prerequisite (not created by this manifest): a kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
25	# secret in the build namespace, named by __PUSH_SECRET__, holding a credential
26	# that may push to the target registry.
27	apiVersion: batch/v1
28	kind: Job
29	metadata:
30	  name: __JOB_NAME__
31	  namespace: build
32	  labels:
33	    app.kubernetes.io/name: image-build
34	    app.kubernetes.io/component: build
35	    app.kubernetes.io/version: "__TAG__"
36	spec:
37	  backoffLimit: 0
38	  activeDeadlineSeconds: __DEADLINE_SECONDS__
39	  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
40	  template:
41	    metadata:
42	      labels:
43	        app.kubernetes.io/name: image-build
44	        app.kubernetes.io/component: build
45	        app.kubernetes.io/version: "__TAG__"
46	    spec:
47	      restartPolicy: Never
48	      automountServiceAccountToken: false
49	      initContainers:
50	        - name: clone
51	          image: alpine/git:v2.54.0@sha256:e8ceedc73bd80992ae8d58a7d24c58b8322146c354f1d2e81a97db4452068ec0
52	          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
53	          args:
54	            - |
55	              set -eu
56	              git init -q /src
57	              git -C /src remote add origin "$1"
58	              git -C /src fetch -q --depth=1 --tags origin "$2"
59	              git -C /src checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD
60	              git -C /src log -1 --format=%ct > /meta/source-date-epoch
61	              git -C /src log -1 --format=%cI > /meta/source-date-iso
62	              git -C /src rev-parse --short HEAD > /meta/git-commit
63	              git -C /src describe --tags --always --dirty > /meta/git-version
64	              echo "cloned $1 at $2: $(git -C /src rev-parse HEAD) epoch=$(cat /meta/source-date-epoch) version=$(cat /meta/git-version)"
65	            - clone
66	            - "__REPO_URL__"
67	            - "__REF__"
68	          env:
69	            - name: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT
70	              value: "1"
71	            - name: GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0
72	              value: safe.directory
73	            - name: GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0
74	              value: /src
75	          # Memory requests are deliberately small: the build node runs at ~98%
76	          # of its request capacity, and a pod asking for a GiB of scheduling
77	          # headroom to do a few hundred MiB of work never schedules there.
78	          # The limits are the real constraint; a request is only a hint.
79	          resources:
80	            requests:
81	              cpu: 100m
82	              memory: 64Mi
83	            limits:
84	              cpu: "1"
85	              memory: 1Gi
86	          # Hardened like any other container: the clone needs to write /src and
87	          # /meta and nothing else, so it keeps no capability and cannot escalate.
88	          securityContext:
89	            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
90	            capabilities:
91	              drop: ["ALL"]
92	            seccompProfile:
93	              type: RuntimeDefault
94	          volumeMounts:
95	            - name: src
96	              mountPath: /src
97	            - name: meta
98	              mountPath: /meta
99	      containers:
100	        - name: build
101	          image: moby/buildkit:v0.34.1-rootless@sha256:f68752a5a94acfcdad2d07867b7075601a421638e17fc5f28efc1c814d0c4f89
102	          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
103	          args:
104	            - |
105	              set -eu
106	              cloned_epoch="$(cat /meta/source-date-epoch)"
107	              if [ "${cloned_epoch}" != "__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__" ]; then
108	                echo "REF __REF__ is commit epoch ${cloned_epoch} in the cluster but __SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__ in the local repository; run git fetch and retry" >&2
109	                exit 1
110	              fi
111	              buildctl-daemonless.sh build \
112	                --frontend dockerfile.v0 \
113	                --local context=/src \
114	                --local dockerfile=/src \
115	                --opt filename=__DOCKERFILE__ \
116	                --opt platform=linux/amd64 \
117	                --opt build-arg:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__ \
118	                --opt build-arg:BUILD_GIT_VERSION="$(cat /meta/git-version)" \
119	                --opt build-arg:BUILD_GIT_COMMIT="$(cat /meta/git-commit)" \
120	                --opt build-arg:BUILD_DATE="$(cat /meta/source-date-iso)" \
121	                --opt build-arg:DOCKER_REGISTRY=docker.io \
122	                --metadata-file /meta/metadata.json \
123	                --output type=image,name=__IMAGE__:__TAG__,push=__PUSH__,rewrite-timestamp=true
124	              cat /meta/metadata.json
125	          env:
126	            - name: BUILDKITD_FLAGS
127	              value: "--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox"
128	            - name: DOCKER_CONFIG
129	              value: "/docker-config"
130	          # Unconfined here is deliberate and is NOT an oversight left over from
131	          # the init containers above: rootless buildkitd with
132	          # --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox needs both profiles relaxed to run
133	          # nested containers. Tightening them breaks every build; the
134	          # unprivileged uid and the dropped capabilities are the boundary.
135	          securityContext:
136	            runAsUser: 1000
137	            runAsGroup: 1000
138	            seccompProfile:
139	              type: Unconfined
140	            appArmorProfile:
141	              type: Unconfined
142	          resources:
143	            requests:
144	              cpu: 500m
145	              memory: 256Mi
146	            limits:
147	              cpu: "2"
148	              memory: 4Gi
149	          volumeMounts:
150	            - name: src
151	              mountPath: /src
152	            - name: meta
153	              mountPath: /meta
154	            # Container-internal path, not a host path: rootless buildkitd writes its
155	            # state to $HOME/.local/share/buildkit inside the image, and needs it
156	            # writable. Not a self-containment violation.
157	            - name: buildkitd
158	              mountPath: /home/user/.local/share/buildkit
159	            - name: docker-config
160	              mountPath: /docker-config
161	              readOnly: true
162	      volumes:
163	        - name: src
164	          emptyDir: {}
165	        - name: meta
166	          emptyDir: {}
167	        - name: buildkitd
168	          emptyDir: {}
169	        - name: docker-config
170	          secret:
171	            secretName: __PUSH_SECRET__
172	            items:
173	              - key: .dockerconfigjson
174	                path: config.json
175

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Resolves BUILD_TARGET into the kubeconfig file and kubectl context that
3	# `kubectl` actually needs, and provides the kc() helper every call goes
4	# through. Sourced by hack/build-cluster.sh; keeping the mapping here rather
5	# than inline means any future caller shares it instead of restating it.
6	#
7	# Defines variables and a function only: no `set -euo pipefail`, no `exit`,
8	# no output. The sourcing script owns all of that.
9	
10	# BUILD_TARGET is either a kubectl context in the default kubeconfig or one of
11	# the build clusters, whose contexts live in their own kubeconfig files under a
12	# name that differs from the one people use for the cluster. Resolve the alias
13	# into the kubeconfig file and context that kubectl actually needs; anything
14	# that is not an alias stays a plain context name. A case statement, not an
15	# associative array: macOS still ships bash 3.2.
16	KUBECONFIG_PATH=""
17	KUBE_CONTEXT="${BUILD_TARGET:-}"
18	case "${BUILD_TARGET:-}" in
19	sun)
20		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/sun"
21		KUBE_CONTEXT=default
22		;;
23	nukedev)
24		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-dev"
25		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-dev
26		;;
27	nukeprod)
28		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-prod"
29		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-prod
30		;;
31	esac
32	
33	# Every kubectl call goes through this, so the resolved kubeconfig and context
34	# cannot drift between the validation and the calls it guards.
35	kc() {
36		if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
37			KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
38		else
39			kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
40		fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Provisions the cluster-side prerequisites for a remote build: the `build`
3	# namespace and the docker.io push secret the Job mounts. Idempotent — running
4	# it twice exits 0 and leaves exactly one namespace and one secret.
5	#
6	# Called by hand before the first `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` against a
7	# cluster. It deliberately creates no Job: jobs are per-build, rendered by
8	# hack/build-cluster.sh, which refuses to run when one already exists.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
12	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/dockerconfig.json.tpl}"
13	
14	BUILD_TARGET="${1:-}"
15	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
16	BUILD_PUSH_SECRET="${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET:-buildkit-push}"
17	
18	die() {
19		echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: $*" >&2
20		exit 1
21	}
22	
23	[ -n "${BUILD_TARGET}" ] || die "usage: $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}") <sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>"
24	[ -f "${TEMPLATE}" ] || die "template not found: ${TEMPLATE}"
25	
26	# The same -teamvault-config value `make apply` takes (Makefile.k8s). Defaults to
27	# the config the repo's own .envrc uses, so an operator who has teamvault-cli set
28	# up does not have to export anything.
29	TEAMVAULT="${TEAMVAULT:-${HOME}/.config/teamvault-cli/config.json}"
30	[ -f "${TEAMVAULT}" ] || die "teamvault config not found: ${TEAMVAULT} (set TEAMVAULT to override)"
31	command -v teamvault-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
32		die "teamvault-cli not found on PATH; it resolves the lookup key in ${TEMPLATE}"
33	
34	# Shared with hack/build-cluster.sh so the alias mapping cannot drift between
35	# provisioning and building.
36	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
37	
38	# The rendered credential lives in a 600 temp file for the length of one
39	# `create secret --dry-run` and is removed on every exit path. It is never
40	# echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo.
41	RENDERED="$(mktemp)"
42	chmod 600 "${RENDERED}"
43	trap 'rm -f "${RENDERED}"' EXIT INT TERM
44	
45	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: cluster ${BUILD_TARGET} (kubectl context ${KUBE_CONTEXT})"
46	
47	kc create namespace "${NAMESPACE}" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
48	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: namespace ${NAMESPACE} present"
49	
50	# The lookup key comes from the template, so the template stays the single
51	# declaration of which TeamVault item and which registry this secret is for.
52	TEAMVAULT_KEY="$(sed -nE 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9]{6,12})" \| teamvaultUser.*/\1/p' "${TEMPLATE}" | head -1)"
53	[ -n "${TEAMVAULT_KEY}" ] || die "no teamvaultUser lookup key found in ${TEMPLATE}"
54	
55	# teamvault-cli, not teamvault-config-parser: the parser takes its password from
56	# the config file, which holds only url and user, so it authenticates unprivileged
57	# and gets 403 on this item. The CLI reads the login from the macOS Keychain.
58	TV_USER="$(teamvault-cli username --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
59	TV_PASS="$(teamvault-cli password --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
60	[ -n "${TV_USER}" ] && [ -n "${TV_PASS}" ] || die "teamvault returned an empty credential for key ${TEAMVAULT_KEY}"
61	
62	# docker.io's canonical auths key, per the template.
63	printf '{"auths":{"https://index.docker.io/v1/":{"username":"%s","password":"%s"}}}' \
64		"${TV_USER}" "${TV_PASS}" >"${RENDERED}"
65	unset TV_USER TV_PASS
66	[ -s "${RENDERED}" ] || die "failed to render ${TEMPLATE}"
67	
68	kc create secret generic "${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET}" \
69		-n "${NAMESPACE}" \
70		--type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson \
71		--from-file=.dockerconfigjson="${RENDERED}" \
72		--dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
73	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: secret ${NAMESPACE}/${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET} present"
74	
75	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: ready — make build BUILD_TARGET=${BUILD_TARGET}"

ARG BUILD_GIT_VERSION=dev

<summary>
- Adds a build-target switch so the image can be built locally (default) or inside a Kubernetes cluster.
- The local build command and the image tag it produces stay exactly as they are today.
- The cluster arm prints the fully composed image reference before it hands off to the cluster runner.
- The cluster arm refuses to run without a caller-supplied tag, so a released tag can never be republished by accident.
- The upload, clean, and publish-all targets stay local-only and are rejected immediately when a cluster target is requested.
- Repository and tag are composed once, so both arms publish to the same image repository and cannot drift.
- No new build knobs are added beyond build target, image, tag, and version.
- The refusal messages name the offending variable or targets before any cluster Job is created.
</summary>

# BUILD_TARGET selects where `make build` runs. `local` (the default) uses the
# local Docker daemon; any other value names a cluster alias (sun / nukedev /
# nukeprod) or a kubectl context and builds inside that cluster as a Job
# rendered from hack/build-job.yaml.
BUILD_TARGET ?= local

# Capture VERSION's origin BEFORE the default below overwrites it. After the
# ifeq block the origin is `file` on every invocation, so a guard written below
# it never fires.
VERSION_ORIGIN := $(origin VERSION)

ifeq ($(VERSION),)
	VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags `git rev-list --tags --max-count=1`)
endif

# Composed once for both arms. Recursively expanded (`=`), because Makefile:3
# includes this file before Makefile:5 assigns SERVICE, so $(SERVICE) is unset
# at parse time.
IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)
TAG = $(VERSION)

ifneq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
# The cluster arm needs a caller-supplied tag. VERSION_ORIGIN is captured above
# the default, so this refuses the git-describe default that would otherwise
# republish a released tag.
ifeq ($(filter command line environment,$(VERSION_ORIGIN)),)
$(error the cluster arm needs an explicit VERSION; pass VERSION=<tag> on the command line or in the environment)
endif

# where a recipe-level `exit 1` would not.
ifneq ($(filter upload clean buca,$(MAKECMDGOALS)),)
$(error upload, clean and buca are local-only; run them with BUILD_TARGET=local)
endif
endif

.PHONY: build
build: check-go-mod
	@if [ -z "$(VERSION)" ]; then echo "ERROR: no VERSION set and no git tag found — set VERSION=vX.Y.Z or create a tag" >&2; exit 1; fi

	docker build \
	--pull \
	--no-cache \
	--rm=true \
	--platform=linux/amd64 \
	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \

	-f Dockerfile .
else
.PHONY: build
build:
	@echo "$(IMAGE):$(TAG)"
	BUILD_TARGET='$(BUILD_TARGET)' \

	REF='$(REF)' \

	IMAGE='$(IMAGE)' \

	PUSH_SECRET='buildkit-push' \

.PHONY: check-go-mod
check-go-mod:

.PHONY: upload

.PHONY: clean
clean:

.PHONY: buca

2	spec: ["001-cluster-build-arm"]
3	status: draft
4	created: "2026-11-09T20:07:41Z"
5	---
6	
7	<summary>
8	- Adds a build-target switch so the image can be built locally (default) or inside a Kubernetes cluster.
9	- The local build command and the image tag it produces stay exactly as they are today.
10	- The cluster arm prints the fully composed image reference before it hands off to the cluster runner.
11	- The cluster arm refuses to run without a caller-supplied tag, so a released tag can never be republished by accident.
12	- The upload, clean, and publish-all targets stay local-only and are rejected immediately when a cluster target is requested.
13	- Repository and tag are composed once, so both arms publish to the same image repository and cannot drift.
14	- No new build knobs are added beyond build target, image, tag, and version.
15	- The refusal messages name the offending variable or targets before any cluster Job is created.
16	</summary>
17	
18	<objective>
19	Change the Docker build makefile so `BUILD_TARGET` selects between the unchanged local arm (`local`, the default) and a cluster arm that dispatches a named commit to the copied cluster runner. Capture `VERSION`'s origin before the existing parse-time default so the cluster arm can refuse a defaulted tag, and reject `upload`/`clean`/`buca` at parse time when a cluster target is set.
20	</objective>
21	
22	<context>
23	Read these files before editing:
24	- `Makefile` — note that line 3 includes `Makefile.docker` before line 5 assigns `SERVICE`.
25	- `Makefile.docker` — the file you are editing.
26	- `Makefile.precommit` — the `make precommit` gate.
27	- `Makefile.variables` — `ROOTDIR`.
28	- `docs/dod.md` — the project definition of done.
29	
30	Reference documentation (in-container paths):
31	- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/go-makefile-commands.md`
32	- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/go-precommit.md`
33	- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/git-workflow.md`
34	
35	The cluster runner `hack/build-cluster.sh` does not exist yet; it is created by the next prompt. This prompt's verification uses `make -n`, which renders the invocation without executing the runner, so that is expected.
36	</context>
37	
38	<requirements>
39	1. In `Makefile.docker`, add the build-target selector at column 0, before the existing `VERSION` default block:
40	
41	   ```make
42	   BUILD_TARGET ?= local
43	   ```
44	
45	   The assignment must start in column 0 so `grep -c '^BUILD_TARGET' Makefile.docker` sees it.
46	
47	2. Immediately before the existing `ifeq ($(VERSION),)` block, capture the variable's origin in a simple-expanded variable:
48	
49	   ```make
50	   VERSION_ORIGIN := $(origin VERSION)
51	   ```
52	
53	   Do not move or modify the existing default block itself:
54	
55	   ```make
56	   ifeq ($(VERSION),)
57	   	VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags `git rev-list --tags --max-count=1`)
58	   endif
59	   ```
60	
61	   The capture must run before that block. After it, `$(origin VERSION)` is `file` on every invocation and a guard written below it never fires.
62	
63	3. After the `VERSION` default block, define the composed repository and tag with recursive assignment:
64	
65	   ```make
66	   IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)
67	   TAG = $(VERSION)
68	   ```
69	
70	   Both must use `=` (recursively expanded), never `:=`. `$(SERVICE)` must appear only here and in recipes: `Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`, so any `:=` or `ifeq` on `$(SERVICE)` evaluates empty.
71	
72	4. Add parse-time guards for the non-local branch, before the `build` target is defined:
73	
74	   ```make
75	   ifneq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
76	   ifeq ($(filter command line environment,$(VERSION_ORIGIN)),)
77	   $(error the cluster arm needs an explicit VERSION; pass VERSION=<tag> on the command line or in the environment)
78	   endif
79	   ifneq ($(filter upload clean buca,$(MAKECMDGOALS)),)
80	   $(error upload, clean and buca are local-only; run them with BUILD_TARGET=local)
81	   endif
82	   endif
83	   ```
84	
85	   These are parse-time `$(error …)` directives, not recipe-level `exit 1`: a recipe-level refusal is invisible to `make -n`, so the acceptance checks could not observe it. The first guard names `VERSION`; the second names `upload`, `clean`, and `buca`.
86	
87	5. Wrap the `build` target in `ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)` / `else` / `endif`.
88	
89	   Local branch — keep the existing prerequisite and recipe, changing only the image argument from `$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)` to `$(IMAGE):$(TAG)` (the resolved value is byte-identical; the tag and command are behaviorally unchanged):
90	
91	   ```make
92	   ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
93	   .PHONY: build
94	   build: check-go-mod
95	   	@if [ -z "$(VERSION)" ]; then echo "ERROR: no VERSION set and no git tag found — set VERSION=vX.Y.Z or create a tag" >&2; exit 1; fi
96	   	DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 \
97	   	docker build \
98	   	--pull \
99	   	--no-cache \
100	   	--rm=true \
101	   	--platform=linux/amd64 \
102	   	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
103	   	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
104	   	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
105	   	-t $(IMAGE):$(TAG) \
106	   	-f Dockerfile .
107	   else
108	   ```
109	
110	   Cluster branch — no prerequisites (the cluster builds a named ref, not the local `HEAD`, so `check-go-mod` must not run). Print the composed reference first, then dispatch the runner with the repository URL and push-secret name as inline literals:
111	
112	   ```make
113	   .PHONY: build
114	   build:
115	   	@echo "$(IMAGE):$(TAG)"
116	   	BUILD_TARGET='$(BUILD_TARGET)' \
117	   	REPO_URL='https://github.com/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer.git' \
118	   	REF='$(REF)' \
119	   	TAG='$(TAG)' \
120	   	DOCKERFILE='Dockerfile' \
121	   	IMAGE='$(IMAGE)' \
122	   	DOCKER_REGISTRY='$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)' \
123	   	PUSH='true' \
124	   	PUSH_SECRET='buildkit-push' \
125	   	TIMEOUT='3600' \
126	   	hack/build-cluster.sh
127	   endif
128	   ```
129	
130	   The `hack/build-cluster.sh` invocation line must begin with whitespace followed by `hack/build-cluster.sh` so `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker` matches an invocation, not a comment.
131	
132	6. Keep the `check-go-mod` target exactly as it is today. It stays reachable only through the local `build` prerequisite.
133	
134	7. Keep the `upload`, `clean`, `apply`, and `buca` recipes exactly as they are today. Do not add a cluster branch to them: the parse-time `$(error …)` in step 4 is the only refusal.
135	
136	8. Do not add any of these variables: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION`, `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, `BUILD_REPO_URL`, `BUILD_DOCKERFILE`, `BUILD_PUSH_SECRET`, `BUILD_NAMESPACE`, `CLUSTER_IMAGE`. The repository URL, Dockerfile path, push-secret name, and timeout are inline literals in the cluster recipe. The only knobs are `BUILD_TARGET`, `IMAGE`, `TAG`, and `VERSION`.
137	
138	9. Keep `DOCKER_REGISTRY ?= docker.io` at the top of the file. The composed reference must remain `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer` when no override is supplied.
139	
140	10. Do not modify any other file. Do not create `hack/`, do not touch `Dockerfile`, and do not touch `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or `.dark-factory.yaml`.
141	</requirements>
142	
143	<constraints>
144	- The local arm's command and its tag must not change. The local `docker build` invocation still produces `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(VERSION)`.
145	- `VERSION`'s explicitness must be captured before `Makefile.docker`'s existing default assignment. After that `ifeq` block the variable's origin is `file` on every invocation, so a guard written below it never fires.
146	- `$(SERVICE)` may appear only in recipes or recursively-expanded (`=`) variables. `Makefile:3` includes `Makefile.docker` before `Makefile:5` assigns `SERVICE`, so a `:=` or an `ifeq` on it evaluates empty.
147	- The local-only refusal for `upload` / `clean` / `buca` is a `$(error …)` keyed on the goal list inside the non-local branch, not a recipe-level `exit 1`. A recipe-level refusal is invisible to `make -n`, so the acceptance checks could not observe it.
148	- `IMAGE`, `SERVICE`, the registry and the tag must each satisfy the runner's character whitelist; no value may carry a newline. Do not introduce a value path that bypasses the runner's checks.
149	- The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not configurable inputs.
150	- Do NOT commit — dark-factory handles git.
151	- Existing tests must still pass.
152	</constraints>
153	
154	<verification>
155	Run these from the repository root; all are container-executable and none executes the cluster runner.
156	
157	```bash
158	# The selector assignment exists at column 0.
159	test "$(grep -c '^BUILD_TARGET' Makefile.docker)" -ge 1
160	
161	# The cluster branch invokes the runner on a recipe line, not in a comment.
162	test "$(grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker)" -ge 1
163	
164	# The local arm is unchanged: docker build, no cluster runner.
165	ROOTDIR="$PWD" make -n build > /tmp/local-build.txt
166	grep -q 'docker build' /tmp/local-build.txt
167	if grep -q 'hack/build-cluster.sh' /tmp/local-build.txt; then exit 1; fi
168	
169	# The cluster arm prints the composed reference and calls the runner.
170	ROOTDIR="$PWD" make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 VERSION=probe > /tmp/cluster-build.txt
171	grep -q 'hack/build-cluster.sh' /tmp/cluster-build.txt
172	grep -q 'docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe' /tmp/cluster-build.txt
173	
174	# The cluster arm refuses a tag it did not receive.
175	if ROOTDIR="$PWD" make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 > /tmp/no-version.txt 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
176	grep -q 'VERSION' /tmp/no-version.txt
177	
178	# The local-only targets are refused at parse time when a cluster target is set.
179	if ROOTDIR="$PWD" make -n buca BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 VERSION=probe > /tmp/local-only.txt 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
180	grep -q 'local-only' /tmp/local-only.txt
181	
182	# BUILD_TARGET leaked into no file outside the dispatch, docs, runner, or spec.
183	test -z "$(grep -rn 'BUILD_TARGET' --exclude-dir=vendor --exclude-dir=prompts --exclude-dir=specs . | grep -vE '(Makefile\.docker|README\.md|CHANGELOG\.md|hack/)')"
184	
185	ROOTDIR="$PWD" make precommit
186	```
187	</verification>

1	---
2	spec: ["001-cluster-build-arm"]
3	status: draft
4	created: "2026-11-09T20:07:41Z"
5	---
6	
7	<summary>
8	- Documents the two build arms in the README.
9	- Shows the exact cluster invocation, including the required commit and tag arguments.
10	- States that the publish-all target and its upload and clean steps stay local.
11	- Explains that the cluster pushes Docker Hub and that the private registry copy is produced by the nuke mirror step.
12	- Records the two parse-time makefile traps that the implementation depends on.
13	- Adds a changelog entry under the unreleased heading.
14	- Does not change any build logic or the lane configuration.
15	</summary>
16	
17	<objective>
18	Add a build section to the README that documents the local and cluster arms, the mirror coupling, and the two parse-time makefile traps, and add a changelog bullet under `## Unreleased` recording the change.
19	</objective>
20	
21	<context>
22	Read these files before editing:
23	- `README.md` — it has no build section today; headings are `How It Works`, `Configuration`, `Observability`, and `Task Contract`.
24	- `CHANGELOG.md` — it already has an `## Unreleased` section; add the bullet there.
25	- `Makefile` — note that line 3 includes `Makefile.docker` before line 5 assigns `SERVICE`.
26	- `Makefile.docker` — the dispatch being documented.
27	- `docs/dod.md` — the project definition of done.
28	
29	Reference documentation (in-container paths):
30	- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/changelog-guide.md`
31	- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/documentation-guide.md`
32	</context>
33	
34	<requirements>
35	1. Add a `## Build` section to `README.md` after `## How It Works` and before `## Configuration`. The section must cover both arms, the mirror coupling, and the two parse-time traps. Use this text as the target content (adapt wording only if necessary; keep the literal strings the verification greps for):
36	
37	   ~~~~markdown
38	   ## Build
39	
40	   The image can be built on this machine or inside a Kubernetes cluster. Both
41	   arms build the same `Dockerfile` and publish to the same repository,
42	   `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`, differing only in tag.
43	
44	   ### Local arm (default)
45	
46	   With no `BUILD_TARGET` set, `make build` runs `docker build` on this machine
47	   and tags the image `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(VERSION)`. The
48	   command and the tag are unchanged. `make buca` (and its `upload` / `clean`
49	   steps) stays local-only: it pushes from this machine and removes the local
50	   image.
51	
52	   ### Cluster arm
53	
54	   ```bash
55	   make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>
56	   ```
57	
58	   `BUILD_TARGET` names a cluster alias (`sun`, `nukedev`, `nukeprod`) or a
59	   kubectl context. `REF` must be a full 40-character commit SHA that exists on
60	   `origin`. `VERSION` must be supplied by the caller: the cluster arm refuses
61	   to run when `VERSION` would resolve from the makefile's own `git describe`
62	   default, so a released tag cannot be republished by accident.
63	
64	   The arm renders a Kubernetes Job from `hack/build-job.yaml`, applies it
65	   through `hack/build-cluster.sh`, waits for it, and reports the Job's log
66	   lines. It pushes `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:<tag>` to Docker
67	   Hub. The private registry copy the deployment pulls from is produced by
68	   nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` step, not by this build.
69	
70	   Before the first cluster build, provision the `build` namespace and the
71	   `buildkit-push` credential once:
72	
73	   ```bash
74	   hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>
75	   ```
76	
77	   ### Two parse-time traps
78	
79	   - `VERSION` is defaulted at parse time in `Makefile.docker` before any guard
80	     can read its origin. The cluster arm captures the origin before that
81	     default and refuses a defaulted tag; a guard written after the default
82	     would never fire.
83	   - `Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`, so
84	     `$(SERVICE)` may appear only in recipes or recursively-expanded variables.
85	     A `:=` or an `ifeq` on it evaluates empty and composes
86	     `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
87	   ~~~~
88	
89	   Do not copy the outer `~~~~markdown` fence into the README; it only delimits the suggested content in this prompt. The nested `bash` fences are part of the README content.
90	
91	   The literal invocation `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` must appear verbatim in the README.
92	
93	2. State in the build section that `buca` (and its `upload` / `clean` steps) remains local-only. The word `buca` must appear in the README.
94	
95	3. State in the build section that the cluster arm pushes Docker Hub while nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` step produces the private copy. The literal `MIRROR_IMAGES` must appear in the README. Do not claim the cluster arm pushes to the private registry.
96	
97	4. Record both parse-time traps in the build section: `VERSION` is defaulted before any guard can read its origin, and `Makefile.docker` is included before `SERVICE` is assigned.
98	
99	5. Add one bullet under the existing `## Unreleased` heading in `CHANGELOG.md`. The bullet must contain the exact lowercase phrase `cluster build`. Use this wording:
100	
101	   ~~~~markdown
102	   - feat: cluster build arm — `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` builds and pushes the image inside the target cluster; the local arm and `buca` are unchanged
103	   ~~~~
104	
105	   Do not copy the outer `~~~~markdown` fence into the changelog. Keep every existing bullet in `## Unreleased` and every released section unchanged.
106	
107	6. Do not modify `.dark-factory.yaml`. It is pre-landed and already carries the measured-working shape: `workflow: direct`, `pr: false`, `defaultBranch: master`, `autoMerge: false`, `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true`, and `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`.
108	
109	7. Do not modify `Makefile`, `Makefile.docker`, `Dockerfile`, or anything under `hack/` in this prompt. This prompt is documentation only.
110	
111	8. Do not add a mirror entry or bump the pin in `bborbe/nuke`. Mentioning the mirror in the README is the only nuke-related change.
112	</requirements>
113

6	---
7	
8	## Summary
9	
10	- This repo's image can currently be produced on one machine only: the Mac.
11	- Its sibling repos can also build their image inside a Kubernetes cluster, unattended, from any committed ref.
12	- Add that second build path here as an arm beside the existing local one, leaving the local command and tag as they are.
13	- The cluster arm builds a named commit as a Kubernetes Job and pushes the result to `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`, the repository nuke's mirror step copies into the private registry the deployment pulls from.
14	- Two supporting edits make the arm reachable: the image must build from a fresh clone with no `vendor/`, and the dark-factory lane config must stop using the shape that is known to lose commits.
15	
16	## Problem
17	
18	`sentry-alert-consumer` runs on nukeprod, and `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` mirrors `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(CONSUMER_TAG)` into `docker.prod.nuke.benjamin-borbe.de:443`. Every image that mirror copies is cut by hand on this Mac today: `Makefile.docker` carries only the local `docker build` path, and `hack/` does not exist. Nothing else can produce this image, so a release while the operator is away from this machine cannot happen.
19	
20	The arm is not a straight copy. Three properties of this repo make a naive paste fail at runtime rather than at review:
21	
22	- **`VERSION` is defaulted at parse time.** `Makefile.docker` opens with `ifeq ($(VERSION),) VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags …) endif`, so by the time any guard could read `$(origin VERSION)` the variable is `file` and an omitted tag silently resolves to the last released tag. A cluster arm that inherited that default would republish a released tag over itself, irreversibly.
23	- **`Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`.** `Makefile:3` is the include and `Makefile:5` is `SERVICE = sentry-alert-consumer`, so any parse-time use of `$(SERVICE)` inside `Makefile.docker` — an `ifeq`, a `:=` — evaluates empty and composes `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
24	- **The image build resolves dependencies from `vendor/`.** The Dockerfile runs `go build -mod=vendor`, `vendor/` is gitignored, and `origin/master` carries no `vendor/` directory. A Job that clones the repo has no `vendor/`, so the build fails before it starts.
25	
26	A fourth property only bites the lane rather than the build, and it was settled by measurement on this repo rather than by reading the docs. `.dark-factory.yaml` on `origin/master` carries `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true`, and a cluster run on exactly that config failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/001-spec-001-docs-build-section.md: no such file or directory` — the same signature recorded on `obsidian-redirector` PR #15. The identical spec run under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` completed all three prompts. So `direct` is the working shape here and `worktree` is the regression, whatever the two older "completed siblings" carry. `autoRelease: false` stays: it keeps the release manual, which this repo wants.
27	
28	## Goal
29	
30	`make build` on this repo produces the image locally exactly as it does today, and `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` produces it inside that cluster as a Kubernetes Job, pushing `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:<tag>` — the repository nuke's mirror step consumes. Both arms work from the same checkout, and the cluster arm works from a fresh clone with no local preparation.
31	
32	## Non-goals
33	
34	- Changing the local arm's command or its tag. Both stay as they are. The shared Dockerfile does move to module resolution, because the cluster arm cannot build from a clone otherwise; the local arm runs the same Dockerfile and is unaffected by how dependencies are fetched.
35	- Pushing to the private registry from the cluster. The `buildkit-push` credential authenticates against Docker Hub only; the private copy is produced by nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` step, not by this build.
36	- Adding a mirror entry or bumping the pin in `bborbe/nuke`. `CONSUMER_TAG ?= v0.1.0` in `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` is already stale against the deployment's `v0.2.5`; realigning it is a deploy-side change, not this spec's.
37	- Touching the sibling repos — they already carry their arms.
38	- Building at release or tag time. This spec adds the capability; *when* a build is triggered is a separate concern. This repo sets `autoRelease: false`, so a green merge cuts no tag.
39	- Extracting the shared build runner into a common upstream template. The files are copied, not shared.
40	- Extra build knobs beyond `BUILD_TARGET`, `IMAGE`, `TAG` and `VERSION`. The copy source also carries `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION`, `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, `BUILD_REPO_URL`, `BUILD_DOCKERFILE` and `BUILD_PUSH_SECRET`. `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` in particular would reintroduce an opt-out on the refusal this spec ships, so it is not copied. The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not knobs.
41	
42	## Alternatives
43	
44	- **Build in GitHub Actions instead.** Rejected: CI here triggers on push or PR to `master`, so it cannot build an arbitrary committed ref on demand — which is the whole requirement. It would also put a second copy of the Docker Hub credential into GitHub secrets, where one already lives in the cluster's `build` namespace.
45	- **Fix the local arm instead.** Removing `Makefile.docker`'s parse-time `VERSION` default would make local builds safer, but it changes the tag the deployment already consumes and still leaves the image unbuildable without this Mac. A smaller change that does not reach the goal.
46	- **Reuse a shared upstream runner.** The five files are copied from `agent-task-executor` and `go-skeleton`, not vendored from a package. A shared template is the right end state, but it is its own change across every repo in the goal's target set; copying first keeps each repo's arm independently verifiable.
47	- **Do nothing.** See the closing section.
48	
49	## Acceptance Criteria
50	
51	- [ ] **The local arm's command and tag are unchanged** — with no `BUILD_TARGET` set, `make -n build` prints the `docker build` recipe and no reference to `hack/build-cluster.sh`; `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack make build` exits 0 and `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:v0.2.5` exits 0 (`v0.2.5` is what `git describe --tags $(git rev-list --tags --max-count=1)` resolves today, so the tag is spelled out rather than left for the verifier to derive). Evidence: both commands' output, the recorded `docker context show` value, the exit code, and the inspected image id. ⚠️ The `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack` pin is what carries the guarantee, not the ambient state: a docker context pointed at `sun` would make a bare `make build` build on the cluster and prove nothing about the local arm.
52	- [ ] **Post-Deploy (Rung-2):** the cluster arm builds and pushes from a fresh clone — `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe-<timestamp>` exits 0, and `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe-<timestamp>` resolves to a digest **equal to the build log's `containerimage.digest`**. Evidence: the exit code, the Job name, the build pod's `spec.nodeName`, both digests, and `docker image inspect` on the same reference failing on this Mac with `No such image` — a stopped daemon or a malformed reference does not satisfy this.
53	  - `deploy_check:` `kubectlsun -n build get secret buildkit-push -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'`
54	  - `deploy_target:` `buildkit-push`
55	- [ ] **The cluster arm pushes to the repository the deploy consumes** — `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` prints `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe` on one line before it calls the runner. Evidence: the printed line alone — the digest half is AC 2's, at AC 2's own tag, so this criterion does not depend on a build that used a different tag.
56	- [ ] **Post-Deploy (Rung-2):** the cluster arm refuses a tag it did not receive from the caller — `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` with no `VERSION` on the command line or in the environment exits non-zero and prints a message naming `VERSION`, before any Job is applied. The refusal fires even though `Makefile.docker` otherwise defaults `VERSION` from `git describe --tags`. Evidence: the exit code, the message, and `kubectlsun -n build get jobs` showing no new Job for that run.
57	  - `deploy_check:` `kubectlsun -n build get secret buildkit-push -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'`
58	  - `deploy_target:` `buildkit-push`
59	- [ ] **`hack/` holds the five files and the cluster branch invokes the runner** — at the merge commit on `master`, `git ls-tree --name-only HEAD hack/` lists `build-cluster.sh`, `cluster-alias.sh`, `build-job.yaml`, `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`, and `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1 on an invocation line rather than a comment. Evidence: the five names and the count. ⚠️ The copied header comments name `BUILD_TARGET`, so a bare `grep -c BUILD_TARGET` passes on a comment alone — the `^` anchor is the probe.
60	- [ ] **`upload` / `clean` / `buca` stay local, refused at parse time** — `make -n buca` prints `docker push` and `docker rmi`; `make -n buca BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` exits non-zero and prints a message naming those targets as local-only. The refusal is a parse-time `$(error …)`, so it fires under `-n` where no recipe runs. Evidence: both outputs and exit codes.
61	- [ ] **The clone builds the image without `vendor/`** — the Dockerfile no longer forces `-mod=vendor`, so a Job that clones the repo builds the same way a developer's checkout does; `grep -c '\-mod=vendor' Dockerfile` returns 0. Evidence: that count plus the successful cluster build above, which is the behavioural half. The exact replacement flag is the implementer's call — Go's default `-mod=readonly` resolves modules without letting the build rewrite `go.mod`, so pinning `-mod=mod` would mandate an implementation choice the criterion does not need.
62	- [ ] **The documented build path and the lane config match reality** — `README.md` shows the exact cluster invocation `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>`, states that `buca` remains local, and records that the cluster pushes Docker Hub while nuke's mirror produces the private copy; `CHANGELOG.md` carries a bullet for this change **under** `## Unreleased`; and `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `workflow: direct` with `pr: false` — the shape that measured working on this repo — plus `defaultBranch: master` and `autoMerge: false`. Evidence: `grep -c 'BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>' README.md` ≥ 1; `grep -ci 'buca' README.md` ≥ 1; `grep -c 'MIRROR_IMAGES' README.md` ≥ 1; `awk '/^## /{s=$0} /cluster build/{print s}' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## Unreleased` (the bare `grep -c '^## Unreleased$'` alone passes at baseline and asserts nothing, and DB 8's bullet is the `cluster build` phrase); and each `.dark-factory.yaml` value is pinned rather than merely present — `grep -c '^workflow: direct$'` = 1, `^pr: false$` = 1, `^autoMerge: false$` = 1, `^autoRelease: false$` = 1, `^autoGeneratePrompts: true$` = 1, `^defaultBranch: master$` = 1 and `^validationPrompt: docs/dod\.md$` = 1, all against `.dark-factory.yaml`. Those read the working tree, so the criterion also requires the change to be **committed**: `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .dark-factory.yaml` exits 0 at the merge commit — otherwise a pathspec commit that skips the config leaves master on the `worktree` shape, and the next spec in this repo hits the same wall.
63	
64	## Verification
65	
66	`REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` throughout — it is a full 40-character SHA, which is exactly what the runner requires.
67	
68	### Row 0 — the lane config (pre-landed and committed before approval; not a prompt)
69	
70	- `grep -c '^workflow: direct$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
71	- `grep -c '^pr: false$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
72	- `grep -c '^defaultBranch: master$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
73	- `grep -c '^autoMerge: false$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 1
74	- `grep -cE '^(autoRelease: false|autoGeneratePrompts: true|validationPrompt: docs/dod\.md)$' .dark-factory.yaml` = 3
75	- `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .dark-factory.yaml` exits 0 at the merge commit — every grep above reads the working tree, not the commit
76	
77	This shape is measured, not copied. On 2026-11-09 the same spec ran twice against PR #25: under `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true` the run failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/…: no such file or directory`; under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` all three prompts completed. `pr: true` is also rejected in combination with `workflow: direct`, so the two halves are one decision. The two older "completed siblings" carry `worktree` and predate the regression — do not cite them as the target shape.
78	
79	### Container-executable — Row 1 (the `Makefile.docker` dispatch)
80	
81	- `grep -c '^BUILD_TARGET' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1
82	- `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile.docker` returns ≥ 1
83	- `make -n build` prints a `docker build` recipe and no `hack/build-cluster.sh`
84	- `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` prints `hack/build-cluster.sh` and the composed `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe` line
85	- `make -n buca BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe` exits non-zero naming the local-only targets
86	- `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` exits non-zero naming `VERSION`
87	- `grep -rn 'BUILD_TARGET' --exclude-dir=vendor . | grep -vE '(Makefile\.docker|README\.md|CHANGELOG\.md|hack/|specs/)'` returns 0 lines
88	
89	### Container-executable — Row 2 (the runner files and the Dockerfile)
90	
91	- `ls hack/` lists the five expected files — **not** `git ls-tree`, because verification runs pre-commit, when the new files are still untracked and absent from `HEAD`
92	- `bash -n hack/build-cluster.sh && bash -n hack/cluster-alias.sh && bash -n hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` — the copied runners parse
93	- `grep -c '\-mod=vendor' Dockerfile` returns 0
94	- `make precommit` — lint, format and vet clean
95	- `make test` — unit suites pass
96	
97	### Container-executable — Row 3 (docs)
98	
99	- `grep -c 'BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>' README.md` ≥ 1
100	- `grep -ci 'buca' README.md` ≥ 1
101	- `grep -c 'MIRROR_IMAGES' README.md` ≥ 1
102	- `awk '/^## /{s=$0} /cluster build/{print s}' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## Unreleased`
103	
104	### Operator-executable (runs on the host after PR merge, spec verification ladder)
105	
106	- `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh sun` — provisions the `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` secret; idempotent, creates no Job
107	- `make build BUILD_TARGET=sun REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) VERSION=probe-<timestamp>` — one real cluster build, Job name, node and both digests recorded
108	- `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:probe-<timestamp>` — the push landed, and equals the build log's digest
109	- `DOCKER_CONTEXT=orbstack make build` then `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:v0.2.5` — the local arm still works
110	
111	## Desired Behavior
112	
113	1. **A build target selects the arm.** `BUILD_TARGET` defaults to `local`. With `local`, `make build` behaves exactly as it does today: it prepares the module cache, it runs `docker build` on this machine, and it tags `$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)`.
114	2. **Any other value routes to a cluster Job.** With `BUILD_TARGET` set to a cluster alias or kubectl context, `make build` prints the composed image reference, then renders the Job template and applies it through the copied runner, passing the repository URL and the push-secret name as literals. It waits for the Job and reports success or failure with the Job's own log lines.
115	3. **The cluster arm needs a caller-supplied tag.** The cluster arm refuses to run unless `VERSION` came from the command line or the environment. It refuses in particular when `VERSION` would resolve from `Makefile.docker`'s own `git describe` default, so a tag nobody chose can never be pushed. The refusal names the variable and happens before any Job is created.
116	4. **Both arms publish to one repository.** The cluster arm uses `$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)` — the same repository the local arm pushes and nuke's mirror copies, differing only in tag, and composed once so the two cannot drift.
117	5. **`upload`, `clean` and `buca` remain local-only.** Given a cluster `BUILD_TARGET` they are refused at parse time, by name, before any recipe runs.
118	6. **The cluster build works from a clone.** The image build resolves its Go dependencies in module mode, so a Job that clones the repo with no `vendor/` directory builds the same way a developer's checkout does. The local arm's `check-go-mod` preparation stays on the local branch only: the cluster arm builds a named ref, which need not be the local `HEAD`.
119	7. **The lane config is the shape that measured working on this repo.** `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `workflow: direct` with `pr: false` — the pair under which a cluster run completed all three prompts here, where `worktree` + `pr: true` failed at prompt-metadata write. `autoRelease: false` keeps the release manual, `autoGeneratePrompts: true` fires the generator, `autoMerge: false` leaves the merge to the reviewer, `defaultBranch: master` names the base and the `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md` gate stays. This change is **pre-landed and committed on the branch before the spec is approved**, so the lane is correct before the agent is ever asked to run.
120	8. **The documented build path matches reality.** The README's build section shows both arms, says `buca` stays local, and records why the cluster pushes Docker Hub while nuke's mirror produces the private copy. The CHANGELOG records the change.
121	
122	## Constraints
123	
124	- The local arm's command and its tag must not change.
125	- `VERSION`'s explicitness must be captured **before** `Makefile.docker`'s existing default assignment. After that `ifeq` block the variable's origin is `file` on every invocation, so a guard written below it never fires.
126	- `$(SERVICE)` may appear only in recipes or recursively-expanded (`=`) variables. `Makefile:3` includes `Makefile.docker` before `Makefile:5` assigns `SERVICE`, so a `:=` or an `ifeq` on it evaluates empty.
127	- The local-only refusal for `upload` / `clean` / `buca` is a `$(error …)` keyed on the goal list inside the non-local branch, not a recipe-level `exit 1`. A recipe-level refusal is invisible to `make -n`, so the AC could not observe it.
128	- The five `hack/` files are copied unmodified from `origin/master`: `hack/build-cluster.sh`, `hack/cluster-alias.sh` and `hack/build-job.yaml` from `agent-task-executor` (its Job spec carries `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, which `go-skeleton`'s does not), and `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` plus `hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl` from `go-skeleton`. Both repositories are public, so a `git clone --depth=1` from inside the container reaches them. `cluster-alias.sh` is required — the runner sources it and fails at that line without it.
129	- The Job template already passes `DOCKER_REGISTRY=docker.io` as a build argument, so the Dockerfile's base images resolve from the public registry inside the cluster rather than from the private mirror. Do not change that back to the mirror.
130	- `IMAGE`, `SERVICE`, the registry and the tag must each satisfy the runner's character whitelist; no value may carry a newline.
131	- `DOCKER_REGISTRY` keeps its `docker.io` default, so the composed reference stays `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`. No `CLUSTER_IMAGE` variable is needed: unlike the pilot, this repo already composes the `bborbe/`-prefixed path the cluster lane pushes.
132	- `IMAGE` and `TAG` are defined explicitly rather than left to the implementer to invent: `IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)` and `TAG = $(VERSION)`, both recursively expanded (`=`), because the runner consumes repository and tag as two separate variables and `$(SERVICE)` is unset at parse time. The dispatch passes both.
133	- `.dark-factory.yaml` keeps every other key verbatim — `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true`, `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`. The change is exactly two lines, `workflow` and `pr`; a rewrite that drops the validation gate is a regression.
134	- `README.md` gains the build section: it does not exist today (headings are `How It Works`, `Configuration`, `Observability`, `Task Contract`), so this spec makes it the in-repo home for the two-arm topology, the mirror coupling, and the two parse-time traps (`VERSION` defaulted before any guard can read its origin; `Makefile.docker` included before `SERVICE` is assigned). The spec dies after implementation; the README does not.
135	- No new scenario. The behaviour is reachable by checks on the rendered invocation plus one real cluster build.
136	
137	## Assumptions
138	
139	These must hold before the cluster AC can pass; none is created by this spec.
140	
141	- The `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` dockerconfigjson secret exist in the target cluster, **and that credential covers the registry the arm pushes to**. It authenticates against Docker Hub, which is why the arm pushes `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`; a private-mirror push fails `401 Unauthorized` after a successful build.
142	- The repo is public, so the Job's anonymous `git fetch` succeeds; the init container carries no clone credential.
143	- `crane` is installed on the host running the ACs.
144	- `REF` exists in the local repository **and on `origin`**: the runner derives `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the local repository, and the Job's init container fetches the ref from the remote. A commit that exists only locally fails at the clone.
145	- The build pod can reach the Go module proxy.
146	- `kubectl` is configured for the target cluster through the alias files `hack/cluster-alias.sh` resolves.
147	- The prompt container can reach `github.com`, so the two copy-source repositories clone. If it cannot, fall back to copying the five files from a local sibling checkout (`~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor/hack/`, `~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton/hack/`).
148	- The draft PR carrying this approved spec is what triggers the watcher (`dark-factory-implement`, polled every 5 min), and the agent pushes its commits to that PR's branch. `master` is protected, so nothing lands there directly.
149	
150	## Failure Modes
151	
152	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
153	|---|---|---|
154	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown cluster or context | The runner fails before applying anything and lists the accepted values | Re-run with a listed target; no Job exists to clean up |
155	| `VERSION` omitted on the cluster arm | Refusal before the Job is created, naming `VERSION` | Re-run passing `VERSION=<scratch-tag>` |
156	| `REF` is a short SHA, or is not in the local repository | The runner dies resolving `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` | `git fetch`, then re-run with the full 40-character SHA |
157	| `REF` exists locally but was never pushed | The clone init container fails: the ref does not exist on `origin` | Push the branch or commit, then re-run |
158	| The clone's commit epoch differs from the locally derived one | The build container refuses before `buildctl` runs and names both epochs | `git fetch`, then re-run |
159	| A Job with the derived name already exists in `build` | The runner refuses and names the existing Job rather than overwriting it | Delete the finished Job, then re-run |
160	| The runner is interrupted after `apply` | The Job keeps running in the cluster while the local invocation exits; the next run then hits the existing-Job refusal | Inspect `kubectlsun -n build get jobs`, read the pod's log, delete the Job once finished |
161	| The build pod cannot reach the module proxy | The Job fails; the runner prints the last 100 log lines and the Job name | Inspect the Job logs; the local arm is unaffected |
162	| The build pod is OOM-killed or throttled | The Job reports `failed`; the pod status carries `OOMKilled` or a CPU-throttling event | Raise the template's limits in the same change, or build locally for that one image |
163	| The registry throttles or rejects the push | The build fails at the push step with the registry's own error | Re-check the `build` namespace secret, then re-run |
164	| A caller-supplied `VERSION` names an already-released tag | No guard — the push replaces that tag irreversibly | Re-push the image from the released tag, then cut a new release |
165	| The built tag is not the one nuke's `MIRROR_IMAGES` references | The push lands in Docker Hub and the mirror copies the stale `CONSUMER_TAG` (`v0.1.0`), so the deployment does not move to the new image | Bump `CONSUMER_TAG` in `bborbe/nuke`'s `sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` — a separate deploy-side change, out of this spec's scope |
166	| The local arm regresses | `make build` fails or tags differently | Revert the arm; the local path is the regression gate |
167	
168	## Security / Abuse Cases
169	
170	- The runner substitutes caller-supplied values into a manifest and into embedded shell, so every value is checked against a character whitelist and rejected for embedded newlines before rendering. Do not add a value path that bypasses that check.
171	- The repository URL and the push-secret name are literals in the dispatch, not configurable inputs. The whitelist constrains the *shape* of a URL, not *which* repository is cloned and built with a mounted push credential; a configurable clone source on this build would let a caller point the credential-bearing Job at another repo.
172	- The build Job mounts a push credential from a `build`-namespace secret and runs with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. The credential is scoped to pushing an image; it grants nothing else.
173	- The build container runs as an unprivileged user with the sandbox profiles relaxed because rootless BuildKit requires it. That relaxation is deliberate and must not be copied to the clone init container.
174	- `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` reads a TeamVault credential into a `600` temp file and removes it on every exit path. It is never echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo. Do not add a logging path that prints the rendered secret.
175	- `VERSION` is caller-controlled and becomes an image tag and a Job name. The tag is whitelisted and the Job name is sanitized to a valid DNS name, truncated, and stripped of trailing separators.
176	
177	## Suggested Decomposition
178	
179	Prompts should be generated in this order — each row is a single prompt with a clear scope.
180	
181	| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
182	|---|---|---|---|---|
183	| 0 | **Not a prompt.** `.dark-factory.yaml` → `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` (the measured-working shape), keeping `autoRelease: false`, `autoGeneratePrompts: true` and `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`, plus `defaultBranch: master` and `autoMerge: false`. Pre-landed and **committed** on the branch before approval. Satisfies AC 8's `.dark-factory.yaml` clause, so no prompt re-implements it. | 7 | 8 (config clause only) | — |
184	| 1 | The `Makefile.docker` dispatch: the `BUILD_TARGET` split, `IMAGE`/`TAG`, the explicitness capture before the default, the composed-reference echo, and local-only `upload`/`clean`/`buca` | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | 1, 3, 4, 6 | row 0 |
185	| 2 | The build path itself: the five `hack/` files and the module-mode image build | 2, 6 | 2, 5, 7 | prompt 1 (the dispatch calls the runner) |
186	| 3 | Docs: the README build section and the CHANGELOG bullet | 8 | 8 | — |
187	
188	Rationale: row 0 is pre-landed rather than prompted because the lane config must be correct **before** the agent is asked to run — a prompt that fixes the config it is itself running under is a chicken-and-egg. With it in place, prompt 1 establishes the dispatch, prompt 2 supplies the runner it calls and the Dockerfile change that lets it work from a clone, and prompt 3 is independent and touches no build logic.
189	
190	## Do-Nothing Option
191	
192	Leaving this repo without a cluster arm keeps one nukeprod watcher's image tied to the Mac. Every rebuild, every release cut while the operator is away from this machine, and every future unattended pipeline needs a human at the keyboard for this one repo — while its siblings build themselves. The cost is not the one build; it is that the automation has a hole shaped exactly like the repo nobody is watching.
193

2	status: generating
3	approved: "2026-11-09T18:15:17Z"

6	---
7	
8	## Summary
9	
10	- This repo's image can currently be produced on one machine only: the Mac.
11	- Its sibling repos can also build their image inside a Kubernetes cluster, unattended, from any committed ref.
12	- Add that second build path here as an arm beside the existing local one, leaving the local command and tag as they are.
13	- The cluster arm builds a named commit as a Kubernetes Job and pushes the result to `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer`, the repository nuke's mirror step copies into the private registry the deployment pulls from.
14	- Two supporting edits make the arm reachable: the image must build from a fresh clone with no `vendor/`, and the dark-factory lane config must stop using the shape that is known to lose commits.
15	
16	## Problem
17	
18	`sentry-alert-consumer` runs on nukeprod, and `nuke/sentry-alert-consumer/Makefile` mirrors `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:$(CONSUMER_TAG)` into `docker.prod.nuke.benjamin-borbe.de:443`. Every image that mirror copies is cut by hand on this Mac today: `Makefile.docker` carries only the local `docker build` path, and `hack/` does not exist. Nothing else can produce this image, so a release while the operator is away from this machine cannot happen.
19	
20	The arm is not a straight copy. Three properties of this repo make a naive paste fail at runtime rather than at review:
21	
22	- **`VERSION` is defaulted at parse time.** `Makefile.docker` opens with `ifeq ($(VERSION),) VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags …) endif`, so by the time any guard could read `$(origin VERSION)` the variable is `file` and an omitted tag silently resolves to the last released tag. A cluster arm that inherited that default would republish a released tag over itself, irreversibly.
23	- **`Makefile` includes `Makefile.docker` before it assigns `SERVICE`.** `Makefile:3` is the include and `Makefile:5` is `SERVICE = sentry-alert-consumer`, so any parse-time use of `$(SERVICE)` inside `Makefile.docker` — an `ifeq`, a `:=` — evaluates empty and composes `docker.io/bborbe/:tag`.
24	- **The image build resolves dependencies from `vendor/`.** The Dockerfile runs `go build -mod=vendor`, `vendor/` is gitignored, and `origin/master` carries no `vendor/` directory. A Job that clones the repo has no `vendor/`, so the build fails before it starts.
25	
26	A fourth property only bites the lane rather than the build, and it was settled by measurement on this repo rather than by reading the docs. `.dark-factory.yaml` on `origin/master` carries `workflow: worktree` + `pr: true`, and a cluster run on exactly that config failed with `save prompt metadata: open prompts/in-progress/001-spec-001-docs-build-section.md: no such file or directory` — the same signature recorded on `obsidian-redirector` PR #15. The identical spec run under `workflow: direct` + `pr: false` completed all three prompts. So `direct` is the working shape here and `worktree` is the regression, whatever the two older "completed siblings" carry. `autoRelease: false` stays: it keeps the release manual, which this repo wants.

28	## Goal
29	
30	`make build` on this repo produces the image locally exactly as it does today, and `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<sha> VERSION=<tag>` produces it inside that cluster as a Kubernetes Job, pushing `docker.io/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer:<tag>` — the repository nuke's mirror step consumes. Both arms work from the same checkout, and the cluster arm works from a fresh clone with no local preparation.
